105	  const gz = await gzipWorldSync(sync);
106	  socket.emit(gz.buffer.slice(gz.byteOffset, gz.byteOffset + gz.byteLength));
107	  await Promise.resolve(); // let the async gunzip settle
108	  await Promise.resolve();
109	}

1	import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";
2	import { PROTOCOL_VERSION, type ServerMessage, type WorldSync } from "@/lib/net/protocol";
3	import { gunzipWorldSync } from "@/lib/net/codec";
4	import type { TicketClaims } from "@/lib/net/tickets";
5	import { createMemoryPersistence, parseSaveBlob } from "./persistence";
6	import { Room, type ClientSink } from "./room";
7	
8	/**
9	 * The room's contracts, exercised through fake sockets against the in-memory
10	 * persistence — every joined client is a scripted sink, every tick is driven
11	 * by hand (no real timers), and the world is a real (small… no — full-size)
12	 * engine. Room construction takes a couple of seconds (worldgen); the suite
13	 * shares one room per describe where isolation allows.
14	 */
15	
16	type Frame = { kind: "text"; message: ServerMessage } | { kind: "binary"; sync: Promise<WorldSync | null> } | { kind: "close"; code: number };
17	
18	function fakeSink(): ClientSink & { frames: Frame[]; messagesOf<T extends ServerMessage["t"]>(t: T): Array<Extract<ServerMessage, { t: T }>> } {
19	  const frames: Frame[] = [];
20	  return {
21	    frames,
22	    send(data) {
23	      if (typeof data === "string") frames.push({ kind: "text", message: JSON.parse(data) as ServerMessage });
24	      else frames.push({ kind: "binary", sync: gunzipWorldSync(data) });
25	    },
26	    close(code) {
27	      frames.push({ kind: "close", code });
28	    },
29	    bufferedAmount: () => 0,
30	    messagesOf<T extends ServerMessage["t"]>(t: T) {
31	      return frames
32	        .filter((f): f is Extract<Frame, { kind: "text" }> => f.kind === "text")
33	        .map((f) => f.message)
34	        .filter((m): m is Extract<ServerMessage, { t: T }> => m.t === t);
35	    }
36	  };
37	}
38	
39	function claimsFor(id: string, wid: string, role: "owner" | "member" = "member"): TicketClaims {
40	  return { sub: id, wid, name: id.toUpperCase(), skinId: null, role, pv: PROTOCOL_VERSION, iat: 0, exp: 9999999999 };
41	}
42	
43	const move = { forward: false, back: false, left: false, right: false, jump: false, sprint: false, crouch: false };
44	
45	async function makeRoom(worldId = "w1") {
46	  const persistence = createMemoryPersistence();
47	  const record = await persistence.loadWorld(worldId);
48	  const room = new Room(record!, persistence, () => 0);
49	  return { room, persistence };
50	}

9	function mulberry32(seed: number): () => number {
10	  let t = seed >>> 0;
11	  return () => {
12	    t += 0x6d2b79f5;
13	    let r = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), 1 | t);
14	    r ^= r + Math.imul(r ^ (r >>> 7), 61 | r);
15	    return ((r ^ (r >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
16	  };
17	}

19	function makeEngine(authority: "local" | "server" = "server"): GameEngine {

21	}

60	`GameShell.playOnline`: ensure a session → `POST /api/worlds/:id/ticket` →
61	`connectNetworkSession(gameServerUrl, ticket)` → mount the game on the

68	can't be boarded online (a mounted pose is server-driven, which would fight
69	the client-owned pose stream); in-flight arrows aren't replicated (only

```
1	# Wire protocol (v1)
2	
3	The client↔game-server protocol, defined in `lib/net/protocol.ts` (single
4	source of truth — this page is the narrative). Versioned as a whole via
5	`PROTOCOL_VERSION`; join tickets stamp it, and a mismatch is refused at the
6	door, so format drift mid-session cannot happen.
7	
8	## Transport & framing
9	
10	WebSocket to the game server's `/ws`. Everything is a JSON text frame
11	discriminated on `t`, except **one binary frame**: the world sync (join and
12	`resync`), which is gzipped JSON — a fresh world's block diff is bytes, a
13	terraformed one compresses >2×. Hot paths (pose/tick) can move to packed
14	binary later without renegotiating anything: the envelope shape is the
15	contract, not the encoding.
16	
17	## Handshake
18	
19	1. Client connects and must send `hello { ticket, protocol }` within **5s**.
20	2. The server verifies the ticket (HS256, 60s TTL, minted by the web API —
21	   see [online.md](online.md)), checks `protocol === PROTOCOL_VERSION`, loads
22	   the room, and answers `welcome` + the binary `worldSync`.
23	3. Anything else → close with an application code (below).
24	
25	A client regenerates the world from `welcome.seed` (bit-identical since
26	worldgen v11 — see [testing.md](testing.md)) and applies `worldSync.changes`;
27	the join payload is KBs, not the 37 MB voxel field.
28	
29	## Steady state
30	
31	**Client → server**
32	
33	- `pose` @20 Hz — client-authoritative avatar movement + live intents.
34	  Clamped server-side (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport
35	  rejection → `forcePose`); accepted movement drives server-side hunger,
36	  distance stats, and fall damage.
37	- `cmd` — a discrete `Command` + the claimed eye pose (applied through the
38	  same clamps before dispatch, so aimed raycasts resolve where the client
39	  looked). Validated against a per-type **allow-list**; local-presentation
40	  commands (pause/debug/camera) never travel. Budget: 60/s.
41	- `chat` (≤256 chars, 3/s), `ping`, `resync`.
42	
43	**Server → client**
44	
45	- `tick { n, ev, pp, mp, day?, self? }` @20 Hz — world events since last
46	  tick (block edits ride these), other players' poses, deadbanded mob poses
47	  (~10 Hz), the day clock every second, and `self`: the private, server-
48	  authoritative delta of YOUR state (inventory/hearts/hunger/xp/effects/…),
49	  sent only on change.
50	- `mobsKeyframe` every 5s (drift correction), `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`,
51	  `container` (open-chest updates), `chat`, `pong`, `forcePose`.
52	
53	Backpressure: past 256 KB buffered, a client's `pp`/`mp` are shed (events
54	and `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.
55	
56	## Reconnect
57	
58	The replica engine outlives the socket. On a **non-fatal** drop the client
59	walks a back-off ladder (`RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS` = 1/2/4/8/8 s), minting a
60	**fresh** ticket each rung (the 60 s TTL kills a stale one) and doing a whole
61	new `hello` → `welcome` → world-sync — a reconnect is an ordinary join on a
62	new socket, not a special frame, so the server's `join` already re-syncs the
63	same room in place. The server closes the player's _previous_ socket with
64	`4003` when the new one lands (see the table). `resync` stays the same-socket
65	path (a client that's still connected but suspects drift asks for a fresh
66	world-sync + keyframe). Fatal closes are not retried; after the ladder is
67	exhausted the client shows the disconnect modal.
68	
69	## Close codes
70	
71	| Code | Meaning                                           | Client retries? |
72	| ---- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
73	| 4000 | bad/expired ticket (or no hello in time)          | no (fatal)      |
74	| 4001 | protocol version mismatch                         | no (fatal)      |
75	| 4002 | room full (8 players) or server at MAX_ROOMS      | no (fatal)      |
76	| 4003 | kicked (owner action, or replaced by a reconnect) | no (fatal)      |
77	| 4004 | idle timeout                                      | yes (ladder)    |
78	| 4005 | server shutting down (redeploy — reconnect after) | yes (ladder)    |
79	| 4008 | slow client (sustained backpressure)              | no (fatal)      |
80	| 1006 | abnormal close (network drop)                     | yes (ladder)    |
81	
82	## Trust model
83	
84	The server is authoritative for the world: every gameplay command executes
85	in ITS engine; clients cannot invent items or edits. The one client-owned
86	thing is each avatar's own movement (clamped, never trusted blindly). The
87	claimed eye pose on `cmd` is the hybrid model's soft spot — acceptable for
88	invite-only co-op, and the envelope already carries what stricter server-side
89	rewind validation would need.
90	
```

  "new_string": "- `tick { n, ev, pp, mp, vp?, prj?, day?, self? }` @20 Hz — world events since\n  last tick (block edits ride these), other players' poses, deadbanded mob\n  poses (~10 Hz), **vehicle poses** (`vp`, deadbanded — a parked boat costs\n  nothing; vehicles never despawn so no absence-pruning), **arrow poses**\n  (`prj`, the full live set every tick — arrows are few and fast, so they snap\n  and prune by absence; one trailing empty `prj` clears the last one), the day\n  clock every second, and `self`: the private, server-authoritative delta of\n  YOUR state (inventory/hearts/hunger/xp/effects/…), sent only on change.\n- `mobsKeyframe` every 5s (drift correction), `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`,\n  `container` (open-chest updates), `chat`, `pong`, `forcePose`.\n\n**Vehicles & mounted riders (v2).** A vehicle's pose (`VehiclePose`: id, kind,\nx/y/z, yaw, riderId) replicates on `vp` and in the join `worldSync` (keyed by\nserver id, so per-tick deltas line up). Arrows (`ProjectilePose`: id, x/y/z,\nvx/vy/vz — velocity so the client orients the mesh) replicate on `prj`. A\n**mounted** rider is the one hybrid-model exception: the server owns their\nposition (`tickVehicles` drives it from their input intents), so the pose\nstream is rejected without a `forcePose` correction, and the `SelfDelta`\ncarries `mountedVehicleId` (on mount/dismount) plus the authoritative `x/y/z`\n(while mounted). The replica adopts that mount state and snaps to the position,\nskipping its own motion integration until it dismounts.\n\nBackpressure: past 256 KB buffered, a client's `pp`/`mp`/`vp`/`prj` are shed\n(events and `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick."

35:- `GameEngine.ts` — owns `GameState`, processes `dispatch(Command, playerId?)` (the id says whose intent it is; the SP shell omits it), advances `step(dt, input?)`, serializes saves, and publishes snapshots (`subscribe`/`getSnapshot`). Randomness is injectable (`rng`), the world size is overridable for fast headless tests, and four options shape multiplayer hosting: `authority` ("local" honors `pause` and freezes the world while the primary player is dead — the single-player feel; "server" ignores pause and never freezes a shared world), `headless` (skips snapshot building — a server room has no React shell), `replica` (a client mirror of a server room: steps only the local player's prediction, cosmetic mining, and the day clock — mobs/spawns/vitals arrive over the wire instead of simulating), and `bootPlayer: false` (construct with an empty players map — a server room before the first join, a replica before its `welcome`; the snapshot stays a stub until `addPlayer` seats the primary). `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` are the join/leave surface (join restores the player's persisted v17 slice; leave serializes it back for the world save); `setPlayerInput(playerId, input)` stores each client's latest intent packet; `applyRemotePose` is the server-side gate on client-owned movement (speed/vertical clamps, teleport rejection, and a synthesized move summary so hunger/stats/fall damage stay server-authoritative); the `routeDispatch` hook lets a session intercept every dispatch — how online play reroutes gameplay commands up the wire while the input controller and UI stay unchanged.
95:- `remotePlayerVisuals.ts` — the **other** players in an online world: one humanoid per non-primary entry in `state.players` (reusing `playerModel.ts`/`playerPose.ts` + the skin palettes), gait animated from observed movement, topped by a procedural canvas name-tag sprite. Names/skins arrive via the `GameRenderer.remotePlayerInfo` lookup (the shell points it at the session roster); pure state-mirroring like `mobVisuals.ts` — the renderer neither knows nor cares that the poses come from interpolation buffers.
117:## Multiplayer client (`lib/net/`)
119:Online play mounts the **same** shell/renderer/audio/input stack on a different engine: `connectNetworkSession(url, ticket)` (`NetworkSession.ts`) performs the hello → welcome → gzipped world-sync handshake, then constructs a **replica** engine (`replica: true, bootPlayer: false` — worldgen from the server's seed is byte-identical thanks to `lib/world/noise.ts`, the world sync applies the block diff/containers/mobs on top). `useMinecraftGame` accepts the session via its `online` option: the replica engine is mounted instead of constructing one, localStorage persistence is skipped (the server owns the world), replicated server events join the local event drain (so toasts/audio/particles treat them like local ones), and `session.afterFrame` runs each rAF.
121:- **Command routing** rides the engine's `routeDispatch` hook: presentation commands (`pause`, toggles, camera) run on the replica; gameplay commands go up the wire as `cmd` envelopes carrying the claimed eye pose (`selectSlot` optimistically does both). The input controller and every UI panel dispatch exactly as in single-player — they can't tell the difference.
122:- **Own movement is client-owned** (the one hybrid concession): the local player simulates normally for zero-latency feel, streaming pose + intents at tick rate; the server clamps (speed/vertical/teleport → `forcePose` snap-back) and owns the consequences (hunger, fall damage, stats). Everything else is server-authoritative — the replica's own mining is **cosmetic** (progress caps just short of breaking; the true break arrives via the block journal), and `self` deltas overwrite the local player's vitals/inventory through the same validators saves use.
124:- **The replica outlives its socket**: a non-fatal drop runs a back-off reconnect ladder (`RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS`) that mints a fresh ticket (the `reconnect` callback → `requestJoinTicket`) and redoes the handshake — a reconnect is an ordinary join on a new socket, re-syncing the same engine in place, so nothing above the session (renderer/HUD/engine) is torn down. `setSimulatedLatency(ms)` injects symmetric send/receive delay for local testing (also `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS`).
```

This closes the first two MP v2 scope-cuts.\n\nVehicles and arrows now travel on their own per-tick channels (`vp`/`prj`)\nplus the join world-sync, copying the mob-pose skeleton: the server collects\nposes (vehicles deadbanded — a parked boat costs nothing; arrows sent in full\nevery tick and pruned by absence with one trailing empty frame), the client\nupserts them straight into state.vehicles/state.projectiles keyed by server\nid, and the existing renderer draws them unchanged. 243	 * registry, so the result is deterministic regardless of which event triggered it.
244	 */
245	export function evaluateAdvancements(player: PlayerState): string[] {
246	  const unlocked: string[] = [];
247	  for (const advancement of ADVANCEMENTS) {
248	    if (player.advancements.has(advancement.id)) continue;
249	    if ((player.stats.get(advancement.stat) ?? 0) >= advancement.threshold) unlocked.push(advancement.id);
250	  }
251	  return unlocked;
252	}

2	import type { GameState, ProjectileState } from "./state";

4	export type SpawnArrowOptions = {
5	  speed: number;
6	  damage: number;
7	  knockback: number;
8	  fromPlayer: boolean;
9	  ttl: number;
10	};
11	
12	// Spawn the arrow a little ahead of the muzzle so the firer never collides with
13	// its own arrow on the spawn frame.
14	const MUZZLE_OFFSET = 0.6;
15	
16	const scratchDir = new THREE.Vector3();
17	
18	/**
19	 * Launches an arrow from (originX, originY, originZ) along `dir`. The single
20	 * launch path shared by the player's bow, ranged skeletons, and the boss.
21	 * Returns the created projectile (handy for tests).
22	 */
23	export function spawnArrow(state: GameState, originX: number, originY: number, originZ: number, dir: THREE.Vector3, opts: SpawnArrowOptions): ProjectileState {
24	  scratchDir.copy(dir);
25	  if (scratchDir.lengthSq() < 1e-9) scratchDir.set(0, 0, -1);
26	  scratchDir.normalize();
27	
28	  const velocity = scratchDir.clone().multiplyScalar(opts.speed);
29	  const projectile: ProjectileState = {
30	    id: state.nextProjectileId,
31	    position: new THREE.Vector3(originX + scratchDir.x * MUZZLE_OFFSET, originY + scratchDir.y * MUZZLE_OFFSET, originZ + scratchDir.z * MUZZLE_OFFSET),
32	    velocity,
33	    yaw: Math.atan2(scratchDir.x, scratchDir.z),
34	    pitch: Math.asin(Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, scratchDir.y))),
35	    damage: opts.damage,
36	    knockback: opts.knockback,
37	    fromPlayer: opts.fromPlayer,
38	    ttl: opts.ttl
39	  };
40	
41	  state.nextProjectileId += 1;
42	  state.projectiles.push(projectile);
43	  return projectile;
44	}

4	import type { EmitGameEvent, GameState, MobState, PlayerState } from "../state";

13	// Scratch vectors — the tick runs every frame over every arrow and must not allocate.
14	const segDir = new THREE.Vector3();

17	/**
18	 * Distance along the unit-direction segment [origin, origin + dir*len] of the
19	 * point on it closest to (px, py, pz), clamped to the segment endpoints.
20	 */
21	function closestParam(ox: number, oy: number, oz: number, dx: number, dy: number, dz: number, len: number, px: number, py: number, pz: number): number {
22	  const t = (px - ox) * dx + (py - oy) * dy + (pz - oz) * dz;
23	  return t < 0 ? 0 : t > len ? len : t;
24	}
25	
26	// A boss body is far wider than the default padding suits, so widen the hit
27	// cylinder for tall mobs; ordinary mobs keep the tight 0.45 padding.
28	function mobBodyRadius(mob: MobState): number {
29	  return ARROW_HIT_RADIUS + (mob.halfHeight > 1.4 ? 0.9 : 0);
30	}

32	/**
33	 * Advances every in-flight arrow. Each arrow integrates under gravity in capped
34	 * substeps so a fast shot can't skip a 1-block wall or a thin mob: per substep
35	 * it sweeps the world DDA for a block hit and tests the segment against the
36	 * relevant entity (mobs for player arrows, the player for mob arrows), resolving
37	 * whichever is nearer. Spent arrows (hit, expired, or out of bounds) despawn.
38	 */
39	export function tickProjectiles(state: GameState, dt: number, deps: ProjectileTickDeps): void {
40	  const { world, projectiles } = state;
41	  if (projectiles.length === 0) return;
42	  const dead: number[] = [];
43	
44	  for (let i = 0; i < projectiles.length; i += 1) {
45	    const p = projectiles[i];
46	    p.ttl -= dt;
47	    if (p.ttl <= 0) {
48	      dead.push(i);
49	      continue;
50	    }
51	
52	    const substeps = Math.min(ARROW_MAX_SUBSTEPS, Math.max(1, Math.ceil((p.velocity.length() * dt) / ARROW_MAX_SEGMENT)));
53	    const sdt = dt / substeps;
54	    let removed = false;
55	
56	    for (let s = 0; s < substeps && !removed; s += 1) {
57	      p.velocity.y -= ARROW_GRAVITY * sdt;
58	      const segLen = p.velocity.length() * sdt;
59	      if (segLen < 1e-9) continue;
60	      segDir.copy(p.velocity).divideScalar(p.velocity.length());
61	
62	      // Swept block collision (reuses the world DDA used for mining/line-of-sight).
63	      let blockT = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
64	      const blockHit = voxelRaycast(world, p.position, segDir, segLen);
65	      if (blockHit && blockHit.distance <= segLen) blockT = blockHit.distance;
66	
67	      // Nearest entity along the segment.
68	      let entityT = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
69	      let hitMobIndex = -1;
70	      let hitPlayer: PlayerState | null = null;
71	      if (p.fromPlayer) {
72	        for (let m = 0; m < state.mobs.length; m += 1) {
73	          const mob = state.mobs[m];
74	          const t = closestParam(
75	            p.position.x,
76	            p.position.y,
77	            p.position.z,
78	            segDir.x,
79	            segDir.y,
80	            segDir.z,
81	            segLen,
82	            mob.position.x,
83	            mob.position.y,
84	            mob.position.z
85	          );
86	          const horiz = Math.hypot(p.position.x + segDir.x * t - mob.position.x, p.position.z + segDir.z * t - mob.position.z);
87	          const vert = Math.abs(p.position.y + segDir.y * t - mob.position.y);
88	          if (horiz <= mobBodyRadius(mob) && vert <= mob.halfHeight + ARROW_HIT_RADIUS && t < entityT) {
89	            entityT = t;
90	            hitMobIndex = m;
91	          }
92	        }
93	      } else {
94	        // A mob arrow tests every player's body cylinder — nearest hit wins.
95	        for (const player of state.players.values()) {
96	          const feet = player.position;
97	          const midY = feet.y + PLAYER_HEIGHT / 2;
98	          const t = closestParam(p.position.x, p.position.y, p.position.z, segDir.x, segDir.y, segDir.z, segLen, feet.x, midY, feet.z);
99	          const horiz = Math.hypot(p.position.x + segDir.x * t - feet.x, p.position.z + segDir.z * t - feet.z);
100	          const vert = Math.abs(p.position.y + segDir.y * t - midY);
101	          if (horiz <= PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH + ARROW_HIT_RADIUS && vert <= PLAYER_HEIGHT / 2 + ARROW_HIT_RADIUS && t < entityT) {
102	            entityT = t;
103	            hitPlayer = player;
104	          }
105	        }
106	      }
107	
108	      if (entityT !== Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY && entityT <= blockT) {
109	        const hx = p.position.x + segDir.x * entityT;
110	        const hy = p.position.y + segDir.y * entityT;
111	        const hz = p.position.z + segDir.z * entityT;
112	        if (p.fromPlayer) {
113	          const mob = state.mobs[hitMobIndex];
114	          mob.hp -= p.damage;
115	          knock.set(segDir.x, 0, segDir.z);
116	          if (knock.lengthSq() > 1e-6) {
117	            knock.normalize();
118	            mob.direction.copy(knock);
119	            mob.position.addScaledVector(knock, p.knockback);
120	            mob.position.y += 0.1;
121	          }
122	          deps.emit({ type: "mobHit", kind: mob.kind });
123	          deps.emit({ type: "arrowHit", x: hx, y: hy, z: hz, target: "mob" });
124	          if (mob.hp <= 0) deps.removeMobAt(hitMobIndex);
125	        } else if (hitPlayer) {

128	          hitPlayer.velocity.z += segDir.z * p.knockback;
129	          deps.emit({ type: "arrowHit", x: hx, y: hy, z: hz, target: "player" });
130	        }
131	        removed = true;
132	      } else if (blockT !== Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) {
133	        deps.emit({
134	          type: "arrowHit",
135	          x: p.position.x + segDir.x * blockT,
136	          y: p.position.y + segDir.y * blockT,
137	          z: p.position.z + segDir.z * blockT,
138	          target: "block"
139	        });
140	        removed = true;
141	      } else {
142	        p.position.addScaledVector(segDir, segLen);
143	      }
144	    }
145	
146	    if (!removed) {
147	      const speed = p.velocity.length();
148	      p.yaw = Math.atan2(p.velocity.x, p.velocity.z);
149	      p.pitch = Math.asin(speed > 1e-6 ? Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, p.velocity.y / speed)) : 0);

152	        p.position.z < 1 ||
153	        p.position.x > world.sizeX - 1 ||
154	        p.position.z > world.sizeZ - 1 ||
155	        p.position.y < 0 ||
156	        p.position.y > world.sizeY
157	      ) {
158	        removed = true;
159	      }
160	    }
161	    if (removed) dead.push(i);
162	  }

3	import {

9	  SPEAR_THROW_LIFETIME_SECONDS,

11	} from "@/lib/game/config";

13	import type { EmitGameEvent, GameState, PlayerState, ThrownSpearState } from "../state";
14	import { lookDirection } from "./playerMotion";
15	
16	const scratchDirection = new THREE.Vector3();
17	const scratchDisplacement = new THREE.Vector3();
18	const scratchClosest = new THREE.Vector3();
19	const scratchToMob = new THREE.Vector3();
20	
21	export function tryThrowSelectedSpear(state: GameState, player: PlayerState, emit: EmitGameEvent, rng?: () => number): boolean {
22	  const slot = player.inventory[player.selectedSlot];
23	  if (!slot?.id?.endsWith("_spear") || slot.kind !== "weapon" || !slot.throwDamage) return false;
24	  if (player.timers.spearThrowCooldown > 0) return true;
25	
26	  lookDirection(player.yaw, player.pitch, scratchDirection);
27	  const position = new THREE.Vector3(player.position.x, player.position.y + EYE_HEIGHT, player.position.z).addScaledVector(scratchDirection, 0.55);
28	  state.thrownSpears.push({
29	    id: state.nextThrownSpearId,
30	    itemId: slot.id,
31	    position,
32	    velocity: scratchDirection.clone().multiplyScalar(SPEAR_THROW_SPEED),
33	    damage: slot.throwDamage,
34	    age: 0,
35	    stuckTimer: null
36	  });
37	  state.nextThrownSpearId += 1;
38	  player.timers.spearThrowCooldown = SPEAR_THROW_COOLDOWN_SECONDS;
39	  player.inventory = consumeToolDurability(player.inventory, player.selectedSlot, 1, rng) ?? player.inventory;
40	  emit({ type: "attackSwung" });
41	  return true;
42	}
43	
44	function segmentHitFraction(spear: ThrownSpearState, displacement: THREE.Vector3, mobPosition: THREE.Vector3, radius: number): number | null {
45	  const lengthSq = displacement.lengthSq();
46	  if (lengthSq <= 0) return null;
47	  scratchToMob.copy(mobPosition).sub(spear.position);
48	  const fraction = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, scratchToMob.dot(displacement) / lengthSq));
49	  scratchClosest.copy(spear.position).addScaledVector(displacement, fraction);
50	  return scratchClosest.distanceToSquared(mobPosition) <= radius * radius ? fraction : null;
51	}
52	
53	export function tickThrownSpears(state: GameState, dt: number, removeMobAt: (index: number) => void, emit: EmitGameEvent): void {
54	  if (state.thrownSpears.length === 0) return;
55	
56	  const survivors: ThrownSpearState[] = [];
57	  for (const spear of state.thrownSpears) {
58	    if (spear.stuckTimer !== null) {
59	      spear.stuckTimer += dt;
60	      if (spear.stuckTimer < SPEAR_STUCK_SECONDS) survivors.push(spear);
61	      continue;
62	    }
63	
64	    spear.age += dt;
65	    if (spear.age >= SPEAR_THROW_LIFETIME_SECONDS) continue;
66	
67	    scratchDisplacement.copy(spear.velocity).multiplyScalar(dt);
68	    const distance = scratchDisplacement.length();
69	    const terrainHit = distance > 0 ? voxelRaycast(state.world, spear.position, scratchDisplacement, distance) : null;
70	    const terrainFraction = terrainHit && distance > 0 ? terrainHit.distance / distance : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
71	
72	    let hitIndex = -1;
73	    let hitFraction = terrainFraction;
74	    for (let i = 0; i < state.mobs.length; i += 1) {
75	      const mob = state.mobs[i];
76	      const fraction = segmentHitFraction(spear, scratchDisplacement, mob.position, SPEAR_HIT_RADIUS + mob.halfHeight * 0.35);
77	      if (fraction === null || fraction >= hitFraction) continue;
78	      hitFraction = fraction;
79	      hitIndex = i;
80	    }
81	
82	    if (hitIndex >= 0) {
83	      const mob = state.mobs[hitIndex];
84	      const kind = mob.kind;
85	      mob.hp -= spear.damage;
86	      scratchDirection.copy(spear.velocity).setY(0);
87	      if (scratchDirection.lengthSq() > 0.0001) {
88	        scratchDirection.normalize();
89	        mob.direction.copy(scratchDirection);
90	        mob.position.addScaledVector(scratchDirection, 0.9);
91	      }
92	      emit({ type: "mobHit", kind });
93	      if (mob.hp <= 0) removeMobAt(hitIndex);
94	      continue;
95	    }
96	
97	    if (terrainHit) {
98	      spear.position.addScaledVector(scratchDisplacement, terrainFraction);
99	      spear.stuckTimer = 0;
100	      survivors.push(spear);
101	      continue;
102	    }
103	    spear.position.add(scratchDisplacement);
104	    spear.velocity.y -= SPEAR_THROW_GRAVITY * dt;
105	    survivors.push(spear);
106	  }
107	  state.thrownSpears = survivors;
108	}

export function serializeStats(stats: Map<string, number>): SavedStat[] {
  const out: SavedStat[] = [];
  for (const [id, value] of stats) {
    if (Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0) out.push({ id, value });
  }
  return out;
}

/** Reads gameplay statistics from a save, dropping non-string ids and negative / garbage values. */
export function restoreStats(save: SavedPlayer): SavedStat[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(save.stats)) return [];
  const out: SavedStat[] = [];
  for (const entry of save.stats) {
    if (!entry || typeof entry.id !== "string") continue;
    if (!Number.isFinite(entry.value) || entry.value < 0) continue;
    out.push({ id: entry.id, value: entry.value });
  }
  return out;
}

/** Reads the unlocked advancement ids from a save (non-empty strings only, de-duplicated). */
export function restoreAdvancements(save: SavedPlayer): string[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(save.advancements)) return [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const id of save.advancements) {
    if (typeof id === "string" && id) seen.add(id);
  }
  return [...seen];
}

On a server the\n   * primary may not exist — per-player attribution of world-event progress is\n   * a known multiplayer refinement; until then a shared world tracks none.\n   */\n  private observeProgress(event: GameEvent): void {\n    const primary = this.state.players.get(this.state.primaryPlayerId);\n    if (!primary) return;\n    recordEvent(primary, event);\n    for (const id of evaluateAdvancements(primary)) {\n      primary.advancements.add(id);\n      this.emit({ type: \"advancementUnlocked\", id, name: ADVANCEMENTS_BY_ID[id].title });\n    }\n  }",
  "new_string": "  private emit = (event: GameEvent, actorId?: PlayerId): void => {\n    this.events.push(event);\n    // Observe progress at the one chokepoint every system already emits through —\n    // but guard against recursion (observing an unlock re-enters emit), and skip\n    // it on a replica: the server owns progression and streams each player's\n    // advancements/stats back via the SelfDelta.\n    if (event.type !== \"advancementUnlocked\" && !this.replica) this.observeProgress(event, actorId);\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Folds a gameplay event into the acting player's statistics counters, then\n   * unlocks any advancement whose threshold the new stats just crossed — adding\n   * it to that player's set (before the emit, so a re-entrant observe is\n   * idempotent) and announcing it (tagged with the player so a co-op client only\n   * toasts its own).\n   *\n   * The actor is: an explicit `actorId` (a kill's killer, a death's victim) if\n   * given, else whoever's per-player step or dispatch is currently running\n   * (`actingPlayer`), else the primary (single-player). A server room with no\n   * primary and no attributable actor scores nothing — correct.\n   */\n  private observeProgress(event: GameEvent, actorId?: PlayerId): void {\n    const actor = this.state.players.get(actorId ?? this.actingPlayer ?? this.state.primaryPlayerId);\n    if (!actor) return;\n    recordEvent(actor, event);\n    for (const id of evaluateAdvancements(actor)) {\n      actor.advancements.add(id);\n      this.emit({ type: \"advancementUnlocked\", id, name: ADVANCEMENTS_BY_ID[id].title, playerId: actor.id }, actor.id);\n    }\n  }"
}

A playerless server room credits nobody.\n    const receiver = creditTo ?? state.players.get(state.primaryPlayerId) ?? null;\n    // Babies drop nothing — only grown animals yield loot. `lootingLevel` is the\n    // *killing* melee weapon's Looting (forwarded by tryAttackMob); indirect kills\n    // (arrows, thrown spears, explosions) pass 0, since Looting is a melee enchant.\n    const drops = credit && receiver && mob.ageTimer <= 0 ? rollMobDrops(mob.kind, this.rng, lootingLevel) : [];\n    if (receiver) {\n      for (const drop of drops) {\n        receiver.inventory = inv.adjustSlotCount(receiver.inventory, drop.itemId, drop.count) ?? receiver.inventory;\n      }\n      // XP on kill, baby-gated like drops; the boss pays a jackpot.\n      if (credit && mob.ageTimer <= 0) awardXp(receiver, xpForMob(mob.kind), this.emit);\n    }\n    this.emit({ type: \"mobDied\", kind: mob.kind, x: mob.position.x, y: mob.position.y, z: mob.position.z });\n    // Drops land straight in inventory (no ground item), so announce them.\n    if (drops.length > 0) this.emit({ type: \"pickedUp\", items: drops });\n    // Defeating the boss is the win condition — fire the one-shot victory.\n    if (mob.kind === \"boss\") {\n      state.victory = true;\n      this.emit({ type: \"bossDefeated\", x: mob.position.x, y: mob.position.y, z: mob.position.z });\n    }\n  };",

Loot, XP, and the kill's\n    // progression all follow them. A playerless room with no killer credits nobody.\n    const killer = creditTo ?? (mob.lastHitByPlayer !== undefined ? state.players.get(mob.lastHitByPlayer) : undefined);\n    const receiver = killer ?? state.players.get(state.primaryPlayerId) ?? null;\n    // Babies drop nothing — only grown animals yield loot. `lootingLevel` is the\n    // *killing* melee weapon's Looting (forwarded by tryAttackMob); indirect kills\n    // (arrows, thrown spears, explosions) pass 0, since Looting is a melee enchant.\n    const drops = credit && receiver && mob.ageTimer <= 0 ? rollMobDrops(mob.kind, this.rng, lootingLevel) : [];\n    if (receiver) {\n      for (const drop of drops) {\n        receiver.inventory = inv.adjustSlotCount(receiver.inventory, drop.itemId, drop.count) ?? receiver.inventory;\n      }\n      // XP on kill, baby-gated like drops; the boss pays a jackpot.\n      if (credit && mob.ageTimer <= 0) awardXp(receiver, xpForMob(mob.kind), this.emit);\n    }\n    // Attribute the death (and its \"Monster Hunter\"/\"Dragon Slayer\" progression)\n    // to the killer so each co-op player earns their own kills.\n    this.emit({ type: \"mobDied\", kind: mob.kind, x: mob.position.x, y: mob.position.y, z: mob.position.z }, receiver?.id);\n    // Drops land straight in inventory (no ground item), so announce them.\n    if (drops.length > 0) this.emit({ type: \"pickedUp\", items: drops }, receiver?.id);\n    // Defeating the boss is the win condition — fire the one-shot victory.\n    if (mob.kind === \"boss\") {\n      state.victory = true;\n      this.emit({ type: \"bossDefeated\", x: mob.position.x, y: mob.position.y, z: mob.position.z }, receiver?.id);\n    }\n  };"

```
36:- `state.ts` — `GameState` holds the **players map** (`players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>`; single-player is the one-entry case) beside the world: mobs, vehicles, and thrown spears as **logical entities with no Three.js objects**, day clock, containers, world timers. `PlayerState` owns everything per-player: avatar pose, inventory/armor/hotbar, vitals, effects/xp/stats/advancements, death/respawn, mining/fishing/vehicle, per-player UI flags, per-player timers, live input. Plus `FrameInput`, `GameSnapshot`, `GameEvent`.
64:**Endgame boss & victory.** A `"boss"` `MobKind` is summoned from a held Cursed Totem via a step in the `placeBlock` precedence (`GameEngine.trySummonBoss`, which seeds placement and refuses if a boss already exists). Defeating it (`removeMobAt`) drops a Dragon Heart, sets the session-only `state.victory`, and emits `bossDefeated`. Boss HP, player-relative bearing, horizontal block distance, and the victory flag reach React through `GameSnapshot.boss`/`victory`; the `boss` object is rebuilt only when one of its rounded visible values changes, avoiding sub-block React churn. Renderer-side hostile health bars are procedural `THREE.Sprite`s attached to each mob model and updated directly from `MobState.hp`, so ordinary mob damage does not enter the React snapshot. A new kind requires entries in all seven exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables (`MOB_TEMPLATES`, `FACTION_BY_KIND`, `MOB_DROPS`, `MOB_XP`, `CALL_INTERVALS`, `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS`, `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS`).
74:**Advancements & statistics.** Progression meta (`systems/advancements.ts`) hangs off the **single `GameEngine.emit` chokepoint** every system already emits through: `emit` pushes the event for the shell, then runs `observeProgress` — `recordEvent` folds it into the `state.stats` counters (a `Map<string, number>`), and `evaluateAdvancements` unlocks any advancement whose threshold the new stats just crossed, adding it to `state.advancements` (a `Set`) and emitting `advancementUnlocked` (the one event type `emit` skips, to avoid recursing). The advancement set is a **declarative `{ stat, threshold }` registry**, so unlock is uniform and adding one is a single row with no logic. Tick-driven display stats (distance, play time) bump directly in `step` via `recordTick`, off the unlock path. Both `stats` and `advancements` persist in save v13 and, like `xp` and unlike `effects`, are **kept across death** (`clearEffects` never touches them). The L-key overlay (`AdvancementsPanel`) reads detail through `GameApi.advancementState()` pulled on render — only the open flag and the unlocked **count** ride the snapshot, so play never churns it with stat values the HUD doesn't show.
87:- **Per-voxel lighting**: the world/glass materials are patched via `onBeforeCompile` (`patchVoxelLighting`) to consume the baked `aLight` attribute — they gate the scene-lit colour by sky exposure (caves go dark) and add block light back as an albedo-tinted glow (torches/lava light the dark). **Day/night needs no uniform and no re-mesh**: the scene sun + hemisphere already scale with `daylight` in `syncDayNight`, so a sky-exposed surface dims at night through the scene lights while caves stay dark regardless. The patch anchors on stable `ShaderChunk` includes; the e2e "renders without errors" smoke test guards it against a Three.js bump.
```

7	 * The online HUD corner: ping while healthy, a banner while degraded, and a
8	 * modal when the connection is gone (the world keeps rendering underneath —
9	 * the player leaves through the button, never a dead-end).
10	 */
11	export default function ConnectionStatus({ session, onLeave }: { session: NetworkSession; onLeave: () => void }) {
12	  const [status, setStatus] = useState<NetStatus>(session.status());
13	  const [rtt, setRtt] = useState(0);
14	
15	  useEffect(() => {
16	    const unsubscribe = session.subscribeStatus(setStatus);
17	    const timer = window.setInterval(() => setRtt(Math.round(session.rttMs())), 1000);
18	    return () => {
19	      unsubscribe();
20	      window.clearInterval(timer);
21	    };
22	  }, [session]);
23	
24	  if (status === "closed") {
25	    return (
26	      <div className="net-modal" role="alertdialog" aria-label="Disconnected">
27	        <div className="net-modal-box">
28	          <p>Disconnected from the server.</p>
29	          <button type="button" className="mc-button" onClick={onLeave}>
30	            Back to worlds
31	          </button>
32	        </div>
33	      </div>
34	    );
35	  }
36	
37	  // A dropped socket runs the reconnect ladder underneath; keep the world on
38	  // screen with a banner rather than a modal — it usually resolves in seconds.
39	  if (status === "reconnecting") {
40	    return (
41	      <div className="net-status net-status-warn" role="status">
42	        Reconnecting…
43	      </div>
44	    );
45	  }
46	
47	  return (
48	    <div className="net-status" aria-live="off">
49	      {status === "online" ? `${rtt} ms` : status}
50	    </div>
51	  );
52	}
53

3	import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
4	import type { NetworkSession } from "@/lib/net/NetworkSession";
5	
6	/**
7	 * Multiplayer chat: a fading bottom-left log plus an input that opens on
8	 * T/Enter (releasing pointer lock while typing) and closes on Escape/send.
9	 * Rendered only for online sessions — single-player has nobody to talk to.
10	 */
11	
12	type ChatEntry = { id: number; name: string; text: string; atMs: number };
13	const LOG_LIMIT = 8;
14	const FADE_AFTER_MS = 8000;
15	
16	export default function ChatPanel({ session, locked, onOpenChange }: { session: NetworkSession; locked: boolean; onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void }) {
17	  const [entries, setEntries] = useState<ChatEntry[]>([]);
18	  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
19	  const [draft, setDraft] = useState("");
20	  // Render-time clock (the compiler forbids impure reads in render): advanced
21	  // by the fade interval and on each arrival.
22	  const [nowMs, setNowMs] = useState(0);
23	  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null);
24	  const nextIdRef = useRef(1);
25	
26	  // Subscribe to incoming chat (the session survives re-renders; effect per session).
27	  useEffect(() => {
28	    return session.subscribeChat((entry) => {
29	      // Mint the id OUTSIDE the updater — setState updaters must stay pure.
30	      const id = nextIdRef.current;
31	      nextIdRef.current += 1;
32	      const item = { id, name: entry.name, text: entry.text, atMs: performance.now() };
33	      setEntries((current) => [...current, item].slice(-LOG_LIMIT));
34	      setNowMs(performance.now());
35	    });
36	  }, [session]);
37	
38	  // Entries fade out; advance the render clock at 1 Hz while any are visible.
39	  useEffect(() => {
40	    if (entries.length === 0) return;
41	    const timer = window.setInterval(() => setNowMs(performance.now()), 1000);
42	    return () => window.clearInterval(timer);
43	  }, [entries.length]);
44	
45	  const openChat = useCallback(() => {
46	    setOpen(true);
47	    onOpenChange?.(true);
48	    if (document.pointerLockElement) document.exitPointerLock();
49	    // Focus after the input exists.
50	    window.setTimeout(() => inputRef.current?.focus(), 0);
51	  }, [onOpenChange]);
52	
53	  const closeChat = useCallback(() => {
54	    setOpen(false);
55	    setDraft("");
56	    onOpenChange?.(false);
57	  }, [onOpenChange]);
58	
59	  // T / Enter opens while playing (not while another overlay owns the keys).
60	  useEffect(() => {
61	    const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
62	      if (open) return;
63	      if (!locked) return; // only from live gameplay — menus own their keys
64	      if (event.code === "KeyT" || event.code === "Enter") {
65	        event.preventDefault();
66	        openChat();
67	      }
68	    };
69	    document.addEventListener("keydown", onKeyDown);
70	    return () => document.removeEventListener("keydown", onKeyDown);
71	  }, [open, locked, openChat]);
72	
73	  const visible = open ? entries : entries.filter((entry) => nowMs - entry.atMs < FADE_AFTER_MS);
74	
75	  return (
76	    <div className={open ? "chat-panel open" : "chat-panel"}>
77	      <ul className="chat-log" aria-live="polite">
78	        {visible.map((entry) => (
79	          <li key={entry.id} className="chat-line">
80	            <span className="chat-name">{entry.name}</span> {entry.text}
81	          </li>
82	        ))}
83	      </ul>
84	      {open && (
85	        <form
86	          className="chat-input-row"
87	          onSubmit={(event) => {
88	            event.preventDefault();
89	            session.sendChat(draft);
90	            closeChat();
91	          }}
92	        >
93	          <input
94	            ref={inputRef}
95	            className="chat-input"
96	            value={draft}
97	            maxLength={256}
98	            placeholder="Say something…"
99	            onChange={(event) => setDraft(event.target.value)}
100	            onKeyDown={(event) => {
101	              if (event.key === "Escape") {
102	                event.preventDefault();
103	                closeChat();
104	              }
105	              event.stopPropagation(); // typing must not move the player
106	            }}
107	          />
108	        </form>
109	      )}
110	    </div>
111	  );
112	}
113

(\n              <button type=\"button\" className=\"roster-kick\" onClick={() => session.kick(member.id)} aria-label={`Kick ${member.name}`}>\n                Kick\n              </button>\n            ) : null}\n          </li>\n        ))}\n      </ul>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"

The server re-checks\n  the sender's ticket `role` (same gate as the owner-wide `setDifficulty`/\n  `setGameMode`), so a forged kick from a member is dropped; self-kick is a\n  no-op. 645	## Playing online
646	
647	Online worlds are shared worlds that live on a server and hold **2–8 players** —
648	private co-op with people you invite, not public matchmaking. Everything offline
649	stays exactly as it is: local worlds never need an account or a connection.
650	
651	**Getting an identity.** The first online action signs you in as a **guest** —
652	one click, no form, from the **Account** panel on the profile screen (or
653	automatically when you accept an invite). Guests are real accounts: the worlds
654	you create and join are yours. When you want to keep them across browsers,
655	**Create account** upgrades the guest in place — your worlds come with you.
656	
657	**Hosting.** On the world list, the **Online Worlds** section appears once
658	you've gone online. **New Online World** uses the same form as a local world
659	(name, seed, world type, mode, difficulty); creating it connects you straight
660	in. Press **Copy invite** on your world's card to put a join link on the
661	clipboard — send it to your friends. Invite links expire after a while; copy a

1	import type { SaveData } from "@/lib/game/types";
2	
3	/**
4	 * Cloud sync for single-player saves: gzipped SaveData blobs pushed to
5	 * /api/worlds/:id/save with a last-write-wins stale guard. Each device
6	 * remembers the `updatedAt` stamp it last saw per cloud world (its sync
7	 * cursor); a 409 means another device wrote in between — the caller pulls
8	 * the newer save and lets the player continue from it.
9	 *
10	 * This module is transport only. Wiring into the world list / autosave path
11	 * lands with the online shell (the same GameShell rework that adds the
12	 * multiplayer world browser), so the sync UX ships in one piece.
13	 */
14	
15	const STAMPS_KEY = "minecraft_cloud_stamps_v1";
16	
17	type StampMap = Record<string, string>;
18	
19	function readStamps(storage: Storage = localStorage): StampMap {
20	  try {
21	    const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(storage.getItem(STAMPS_KEY) ?? "{}");
22	    if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== "object") return {};
23	    const out: StampMap = {};
24	    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(parsed)) if (typeof value === "string") out[key] = value;
25	    return out;
26	  } catch {
27	    return {};
28	  }
29	}
30	
31	function writeStamp(cloudWorldId: string, stamp: string, storage: Storage = localStorage): void {
32	  const stamps = readStamps(storage);
33	  stamps[cloudWorldId] = stamp;
34	  storage.setItem(STAMPS_KEY, JSON.stringify(stamps));
35	}
36	
37	export async function gzipJson(value: unknown): Promise<Uint8Array> {
38	  const stream = new Blob([JSON.stringify(value)]).stream().pipeThrough(new CompressionStream("gzip"));
39	  return new Uint8Array(await new Response(stream).arrayBuffer());
40	}
41	
42	export async function gunzipJson<T>(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<T> {
43	  const stream = new Blob([bytes as BlobPart]).stream().pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream("gzip"));
44	  return (await new Response(stream).json()) as T;
45	}
46	
47	export type PushResult = "saved" | "conflict" | "error";
48	
49	/** Uploads a save; "conflict" means another device wrote first — pull before retrying. */
50	export async function pushSave(cloudWorldId: string, save: SaveData, storage: Storage = localStorage): Promise<PushResult> {
51	  try {
52	    const body = await gzipJson(save);
53	    const base = readStamps(storage)[cloudWorldId] ?? "";
54	    const response = await fetch(`/api/worlds/${cloudWorldId}/save`, {
55	      method: "PUT",
56	      headers: {
57	        "content-type": "application/gzip",
58	        "x-save-version": String(save.version),
59	        "x-base-updated-at": base
60	      },
61	      body: body as unknown as BodyInit
62	    });
63	    if (response.status === 409) return "conflict";
64	    if (!response.ok) return "error";
65	    const { updatedAt } = (await response.json()) as { updatedAt: string };
66	    writeStamp(cloudWorldId, updatedAt, storage);
67	    return "saved";
68	  } catch {
69	    return "error";
70	  }
71	}
72	
73	/** Downloads the latest cloud save (null when the world has no blob yet). Advances the sync cursor. */
74	export async function pullSave(cloudWorldId: string, storage: Storage = localStorage): Promise<SaveData | null> {
75	  try {
76	    const response = await fetch(`/api/worlds/${cloudWorldId}/save`);
77	    if (!response.ok) return null;
78	    const stamp = response.headers.get("x-updated-at");
79	    const save = await gunzipJson<SaveData>(new Uint8Array(await response.arrayBuffer()));
80	    if (stamp) writeStamp(cloudWorldId, stamp, storage);
81	    return save;
82	  } catch {
83	    return null;
84	  }
85	}
86

2	 * Worlds — the second level of the save hierarchy. Each world belongs to one
3	 * profile (`profileId`) and owns a single bundled SaveData blob under its own
4	 * `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key (read/written with the existing
5	 * lib/game/save.ts helpers). The world *index* — names, seeds, ordering — lives
6	 * in one versioned manifest blob; the heavy per-world saves stay separate so
7	 * the index reads cheaply.
8	 *
9	 * A world's `seed` is resolved once at creation and is the source of truth for
10	 * regeneration; `worldgenVersion` records the WORLDGEN_VERSION it was generated
11	 * under so a future baseline bump can discard its stale block-diffs.
12	 */
13	
14	import { isWorldType, type WorldType } from "@/lib/world";
15	import { isGameMode, type GameMode } from "./gameModes";
16	import { isDifficulty, type Difficulty } from "./difficulties";
17	import { WORLDGEN_VERSION } from "./config";
18	import { readManifestRaw, resolveDeps, sanitizeName, writeManifest, type ManifestDeps } from "./manifest";
19	import { getProfile } from "./profiles";
20	
21	export type WorldMeta = {
22	  id: string;
23	  profileId: string;
24	  name: string;
25	  seed: number;
26	  worldType: WorldType;
27	  /** Initial game mode, chosen at creation. The *current* mode (switchable in-game) lives in the save blob. */
28	  gameMode: GameMode;
29	  /** Initial difficulty, chosen at creation. The *current* difficulty (switchable in-game) lives in the save blob. */
30	  difficulty: Difficulty;
31	  /** Hardcore world: forces Survival + Hard and permadeath. Immutable for the world's life (unlike gameMode/difficulty). */
32	  hardcore: boolean;
33	  worldgenVersion: number;
34	  createdAt: number;
35	  lastPlayedAt: number;
36	};
37	
38	/** UI metadata for the world-type picker (the engine side lives in lib/world/worldTypes.ts). */
39	export const WORLD_TYPE_PRESETS: ReadonlyArray<{ id: WorldType; label: string; blurb: string }> = [
40	  { id: "default", label: "Default", blurb: "Balanced terrain, every biome" },
41	  { id: "flat", label: "Superflat", blurb: "Level ground — a builder's canvas" },
42	  { id: "amplified", label: "Amplified", blurb: "Towering, dramatic relief" },
43	  { id: "islands", label: "Islands", blurb: "Scattered land in a wide sea" }
44	];
45	
46	export type WorldsManifest = {
47	  version: 1;
48	  worlds: WorldMeta[];
49	};
50	
51	export const WORLDS_KEY = "minecraft_worlds_v1";
52	export const WORLD_SAVE_PREFIX = "minecraft_world_save_";
53	export const MAX_WORLD_NAME = 32;
54	export const DEFAULT_WORLD_NAME = "New World";
55	export const MAX_SEED = 2147483647;
56	
57	export const DEFAULT_WORLDS_MANIFEST: WorldsManifest = { version: 1, worlds: [] };
58	
59	/** The per-world SaveData key handed to readSave/writeSave. */
60	export function worldSaveKey(worldId: string): string {
61	  return WORLD_SAVE_PREFIX + worldId;
62	}
63	
64	/** FNV-1a hash of a text seed into a stable non-negative 31-bit integer (Minecraft-style). */
65	export function hashStringToSeed(text: string): number {
66	  let hash = 0x811c9dc5;
67	  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i += 1) {
68	    hash ^= text.charCodeAt(i);
69	    hash = Math.imul(hash, 0x01000193);
70	  }
71	  return Math.abs(hash | 0) % MAX_SEED;
72	}
73	
74	/**
75	 * Resolves a user seed input to an integer in 0..MAX_SEED-1: blank → random
76	 * (same entropy the engine used for a fresh world), numeric text → clamped int,
77	 * any other text → stable hash. `rng` is injectable for deterministic tests.
78	 */
79	export function resolveSeed(seedInput: string | null, rng: () => number = Math.random): number {
80	  const trimmed = (seedInput ?? "").trim();
81	  if (trimmed === "") return Math.floor(rng() * MAX_SEED);
82	  const asNumber = Number(trimmed);
83	  if (Number.isFinite(asNumber)) return Math.floor(Math.abs(asNumber)) % MAX_SEED;
84	  return hashStringToSeed(trimmed);
85	}
86	
87	/** Coerces one raw entry into a valid WorldMeta, or null if it can't be salvaged. */
88	function sanitizeWorld(raw: unknown): WorldMeta | null {
89	  if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object") return null;
90	  const entry = raw as Record<string, unknown>;
91	  if (typeof entry.id !== "string" || entry.id.length === 0) return null;
92	  if (typeof entry.profileId !== "string" || entry.profileId.length === 0) return null;
93	  if (typeof entry.seed !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(entry.seed)) return null;
94	  const num = (value: unknown, fallback: number) => (typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value) ? value : fallback);
95	  // Hardcore is the source of truth — keep the persisted mode/difficulty consistent
96	  // with it (the engine forces them at runtime, but the meta drives the UI/card too).
97	  const hardcore = entry.hardcore === true;
98	  return {
99	    id: entry.id,
100	    profileId: entry.profileId,
101	    name: sanitizeName(entry.name, DEFAULT_WORLD_NAME, MAX_WORLD_NAME),
102	    seed: Math.floor(entry.seed),
103	    worldType: isWorldType(entry.worldType) ? entry.worldType : "default",
104	    gameMode: hardcore ? "survival" : isGameMode(entry.gameMode) ? entry.gameMode : "survival",
105	    difficulty: hardcore ? "hard" : isDifficulty(entry.difficulty) ? entry.difficulty : "normal",
106	    hardcore,
107	    worldgenVersion: num(entry.worldgenVersion, WORLDGEN_VERSION),
108	    createdAt: num(entry.createdAt, 0),
109	    lastPlayedAt: num(entry.lastPlayedAt, 0)
110	  };
111	}
112	
113	/** Reads the worlds manifest, dropping malformed entries. Never throws. */
114	export function readWorlds(storage: Storage = localStorage): WorldsManifest {
115	  const raw = readManifestRaw(WORLDS_KEY, storage) as Partial<WorldsManifest> | null;
116	  // Only the current manifest version is understood; an unknown version falls
117	  // back to the default rather than risk misreading an incompatible payload.
118	  if (!raw || raw.version !== 1 || !Array.isArray(raw.worlds)) return { ...DEFAULT_WORLDS_MANIFEST };
119	  return { version: 1, worlds: raw.worlds.map(sanitizeWorld).filter((w): w is WorldMeta => w !== null) };
120	}
121	
122	export function getWorld(id: string, storage: Storage = localStorage): WorldMeta | null {
123	  return readWorlds(storage).worlds.find((w) => w.id === id) ?? null;
124	}
125	
126	/** A profile's worlds, most-recently-played first (ties broken by creation time). */
127	export function worldsForProfile(profileId: string, storage: Storage = localStorage): WorldMeta[] {
128	  return readWorlds(storage)
129	    .worlds.filter((w) => w.profileId === profileId)
130	    .sort((a, b) => b.lastPlayedAt - a.lastPlayedAt || b.createdAt - a.createdAt);
131	}
132	
133	/** Creates a world for an existing profile, persists it, and returns it (throws on an unknown profile). `deps.rng` seeds blank-input worlds; `deps.worldType` picks the generation preset; `deps.gameMode`/`deps.difficulty` pick the initial mode/difficulty; `deps.hardcore` flags a permadeath world. */
134	export function createWorld(
135	  profileId: string,
136	  name: string,
137	  seedInput: string | null,
138	  deps: ManifestDeps & { rng?: () => number; worldType?: WorldType; gameMode?: GameMode; difficulty?: Difficulty; hardcore?: boolean } = {}
139	): WorldMeta {
140	  const { storage, now, uid } = resolveDeps(deps);
141	  // Worlds must belong to a real profile — refuse to persist an orphan record.
142	  if (!getProfile(profileId, storage)) throw new Error(`createWorld: unknown profile "${profileId}"`);
143	  const createdAt = now();
144	  // Hardcore forces Survival + Hard, so the persisted meta is consistent from birth.
145	  const hardcore = deps.hardcore === true;
146	  const world: WorldMeta = {
147	    id: uid(),
148	    profileId,
149	    name: sanitizeName(name, DEFAULT_WORLD_NAME, MAX_WORLD_NAME),
150	    seed: resolveSeed(seedInput, deps.rng ?? Math.random),
151	    worldType: isWorldType(deps.worldType) ? deps.worldType : "default",
152	    gameMode: hardcore ? "survival" : isGameMode(deps.gameMode) ? deps.gameMode : "survival",
153	    difficulty: hardcore ? "hard" : isDifficulty(deps.difficulty) ? deps.difficulty : "normal",
154	    hardcore,
155	    worldgenVersion: WORLDGEN_VERSION,
156	    createdAt,
157	    lastPlayedAt: createdAt
158	  };
159	  const manifest = readWorlds(storage);
160	  writeManifest(WORLDS_KEY, { version: 1, worlds: [...manifest.worlds, world] }, storage);
161	  return world;
162	}
163	
164	export function renameWorld(id: string, name: string, storage: Storage = localStorage): WorldsManifest {
165	  const manifest = readWorlds(storage);
166	  const next: WorldsManifest = {
167	    version: 1,
168	    worlds: manifest.worlds.map((w) => (w.id === id ? { ...w, name: sanitizeName(name, w.name, MAX_WORLD_NAME) } : w))
169	  };
170	  writeManifest(WORLDS_KEY, next, storage);
171	  return next;
172	}
173	
174	/** Bumps a world's `lastPlayedAt` so it sorts to the top of its profile's list. */
175	export function touchWorld(id: string, deps: ManifestDeps = {}): WorldsManifest {
176	  const { storage, now } = resolveDeps(deps);
177	  const manifest = readWorlds(storage);
178	  const next: WorldsManifest = {
179	    version: 1,
180	    worlds: manifest.worlds.map((w) => (w.id === id ? { ...w, lastPlayedAt: now() } : w))
181	  };
182	  writeManifest(WORLDS_KEY, next, storage);
183	  return next;
184	}
185	
186	/** Removes a world from the index and deletes its save blob. */
187	export function deleteWorld(id: string, storage: Storage = localStorage): WorldsManifest {
188	  const manifest = readWorlds(storage);
189	  const next: WorldsManifest = { version: 1, worlds: manifest.worlds.filter((w) => w.id !== id) };
190	  writeManifest(WORLDS_KEY, next, storage);
191	  try {
192	    storage.removeItem(worldSaveKey(id));
193	  } catch {
194	    // A failed blob cleanup just leaves an orphaned key; the index no longer references it.
195	  }
196	  return next;
197	}
198	
199	/** Cascade for profile deletion: removes every world of a profile and its save blobs. */
200	export function deleteWorldsForProfile(profileId: string, storage: Storage = localStorage): WorldsManifest {
201	  const manifest = readWorlds(storage);
202	  const doomed = manifest.worlds.filter((w) => w.profileId === profileId);
203	  const next: WorldsManifest = { version: 1, worlds: manifest.worlds.filter((w) => w.profileId !== profileId) };
204	  writeManifest(WORLDS_KEY, next, storage);
205	  for (const world of doomed) {
206	    try {
207	      storage.removeItem(worldSaveKey(world.id));
208	    } catch {
209	      // Orphaned blob; the index no longer references it.
210	    }
211	  }
212	  return next;
213	}

export type WorldSummary = {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  kind: "sp-cloud" | "mp";
  seed: number;
  worldType: string;
  gameMode: string;
  difficulty: string;
  hardcore: boolean;
  worldgenVersion: number;
  role: "owner" | "member";
  updatedAt: string;
};

type Failure = { ok: false; error: "not-found" | "forbidden" | "conflict" | "invalid" | "expired" };
const fail = (error: Failure["error"]): Failure => ({ ok: false, error });

function toSummary(world: typeof schema.worlds.$inferSelect, role: "owner" | "member"): WorldSummary {
  return {
    id: world.id,
    name: world.name,
    kind: world.kind,
    seed: world.seed,
    worldType: world.worldType,
    gameMode: world.gameMode,
    difficulty: world.difficulty,
    hardcore: world.hardcore,
    worldgenVersion: world.worldgenVersion,
    role,
    updatedAt: world.updatedAt.toISOString()
  };
}

/** The caller's membership row for a world, or null. */
async function membership(db: Db, userId: string, worldId: string) {
  const rows = await db
    .select()
    .from(schema.worldMembers)
    .where(and(eq(schema.worldMembers.worldId, worldId), eq(schema.worldMembers.userId, userId)));
  return rows[0] ?? null;
}

15	/**
16	 * Top-level menu shell. Owns the screen state machine (profile-select ->
17	 * world-select -> play) and boots the legacy migration once on mount. The play
18	 * screen mounts MinecraftGame keyed by world id + a reload nonce, so switching
19	 * worlds (or Load/Reset) remounts the subtree — the game effect's cleanup
20	 * disposes the old engine/renderer and a fresh mount boots the next world, with
21	 * no page reload.
22	 */
23	type Screen =
24	  | { name: "profile-select" }
25	  | { name: "world-select"; profileId: string }
26	  | { name: "play"; profileId: string; worldId: string }
27	  | { name: "play-online"; profileId: string; world: OnlineWorld; session: NetworkSession };
28	
29	/** Online worlds mount the same game subtree; the meta is a projection of the server row. */
30	function onlineWorldMeta(world: OnlineWorld, profileId: string): WorldMeta {
31	  return {
32	    id: `online:${world.id}`,
33	    profileId,
34	    name: world.name,
35	    seed: world.seed,
36	    worldType: world.worldType as WorldMeta["worldType"],
37	    gameMode: world.gameMode as WorldMeta["gameMode"],
38	    difficulty: world.difficulty as WorldMeta["difficulty"],
39	    hardcore: world.hardcore,
40	    worldgenVersion: world.worldgenVersion,
41	    createdAt: 0,
42	    lastPlayedAt: 0
43	  };
44	}
45	
46	/**
47	 * Remembers the world being played for this tab so a reload resumes it instead
48	 * of dropping back to the menu. sessionStorage (not localStorage) so a brand-new
49	 * tab still cold-starts at profile-select.
50	 */
51	const SESSION_KEY = "monecraft_active_session";
52	
53	function readSessionPointer(): { profileId: string; worldId: string } | null {
54	  try {
55	    const raw = sessionStorage.getItem(SESSION_KEY);
56	    if (!raw) return null;
57	    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as { profileId?: unknown; worldId?: unknown };
58	    if (typeof parsed?.profileId === "string" && typeof parsed?.worldId === "string") {
59	      return { profileId: parsed.profileId, worldId: parsed.worldId };
60	    }
61	    return null;
62	  } catch {
63	    return null;
64	  }
65	}
66	
67	function writeSessionPointer(pointer: { profileId: string; worldId: string } | null): void {
68	  try {
69	    if (pointer) sessionStorage.setItem(SESSION_KEY, JSON.stringify(pointer));
70	    else sessionStorage.removeItem(SESSION_KEY);
71	  } catch {
72	    // No resume across reload if sessionStorage is unavailable — never fatal.
73	  }
74	}

76	export default function GameShell() {
77	  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
78	  const [screen, setScreen] = useState<Screen>({ name: "profile-select" });
79	  const [reloadNonce, setReloadNonce] = useState(0);
80	  const [connecting, setConnecting] = useState<string | null>(null);
81	  const [connectError, setConnectError] = useState<string | null>(null);
82	  // A join is in flight — guards against a double-click opening (and leaking) a
83	  // second socket. A ref, not `connecting`, so it's set synchronously.
84	  const joiningRef = useRef(false);
85	
86	  /** Guest-or-account → ticket → socket → replica sync → play. */
87	  const playOnline = async (profileId: string, world: OnlineWorld) => {
88	    if (joiningRef.current) return; // a join is already in flight
89	    joiningRef.current = true;
90	    setConnectError(null);
91	    setConnecting(world.name);
92	    try {
93	      if (!(await ensureSignedIn())) throw new Error("sign-in failed");
94	      const grant = await requestJoinTicket(world.id);
95	      if (!grant) throw new Error("could not get a join ticket (is the game server configured?)");
96	      // The reconnect ladder mints a fresh short-lived ticket each retry — the
97	      // 60 s TTL means a stale one is useless a minute after a drop.
98	      const session = await connectNetworkSession(grant.gameServerUrl, grant.ticket, undefined, {
99	        reconnect: async () => {
100	          const next = await requestJoinTicket(world.id);
101	          return next ? { url: next.gameServerUrl, ticket: next.ticket } : null;
102	        }
103	      });
104	      setScreen({ name: "play-online", profileId, world, session });
105	    } catch (error) {
106	      setConnectError(error instanceof Error ? error.message : "connection failed");
107	    } finally {
108	      setConnecting(null);
109	      joiningRef.current = false;
110	    }
111	  };
112	
113	  useEffect(() => {
114	    installUiTiles(); // the menu chrome shares the in-game noise tiles
115	    migrateLegacySave();
116	    // Resume the tab's world if one was being played and still exists.
117	    const pointer = readSessionPointer();
118	    const resume: Screen | null =
119	      pointer && getProfile(pointer.profileId) && getWorld(pointer.worldId) ? { name: "play", profileId: pointer.profileId, worldId: pointer.worldId } : null;
120	    // Microtask hop keeps this off the synchronous effect path (cascading-render lint).
121	    queueMicrotask(() => {
122	      if (resume) setScreen(resume);
123	      setReady(true);
124	    });
125	  }, []);
126	
127	  // localStorage is read below; hold the neutral frame until we're client-side.
128	  if (!ready) return <div className="menu-screen" />;
129	
130	  if (screen.name === "play") {
131	    const profile = getProfile(screen.profileId);
132	    const world = getWorld(screen.worldId);
133	    // Both exist in normal flow; a cross-tab delete drops us back to a menu.
134	    if (profile && world) {
135	      return (
136	        <MinecraftGame
137	          key={`${world.id}:${reloadNonce}`}
138	          world={world}
139	          profile={profile}
140	          onQuitToWorlds={() => {
141	            writeSessionPointer(null);
142	            setScreen({ name: "world-select", profileId: profile.id });
143	          }}
144	          onDeleteWorld={() => {
145	            deleteWorld(world.id); // hardcore Game Over: erase the dead world and leave
146	            writeSessionPointer(null);
147	            setScreen({ name: "world-select", profileId: profile.id });
148	          }}
149	          onReloadWorld={() => setReloadNonce((nonce) => nonce + 1)}
150	        />
151	      );
152	    }
153	  }
154	
155	  if (screen.name === "play-online") {
156	    const profile = getProfile(screen.profileId);
157	    if (profile) {
158	      return (
159	        <MinecraftGame
160	          key={`online:${screen.world.id}`}
161	          world={onlineWorldMeta(screen.world, profile.id)}
162	          profile={profile}
163	          online={screen.session}
164	          onQuitToWorlds={() => setScreen({ name: "world-select", profileId: profile.id })}
165	          onDeleteWorld={() => {
166	            // Hardcore game-over: actually delete the shared world on the server
167	            // (owner-gated; a member just leaves), then return to the list.
168	            screen.session.dispose();
169	            void deleteOnlineWorld(screen.world.id);
170	            setScreen({ name: "world-select", profileId: profile.id });
171	          }}
172	          onReloadWorld={() => setScreen({ name: "world-select", profileId: profile.id })}
173	        />
174	      );
175	    }
176	  }
177	
178	  if (screen.name === "world-select") {
179	    const profile = getProfile(screen.profileId);
180	    if (profile) {
181	      return (
182	        <>
183	          <WorldSelect
184	            profile={profile}
185	            onPlay={(worldId) => {
186	              touchWorld(worldId);
187	              writeSessionPointer({ profileId: profile.id, worldId });
188	              setScreen({ name: "play", profileId: profile.id, worldId });
189	            }}
190	            onPlayOnline={(world) => void playOnline(profile.id, world)}
191	            onBack={() => setScreen({ name: "profile-select" })}
192	          />
193	          {connecting && (
194	            <div className="net-modal" role="status">
195	              <div className="net-modal-box">Joining “{connecting}”…</div>
196	            </div>
197	          )}
198	          {connectError && (
199	            <div className="net-modal" role="alertdialog" aria-label="Connection failed">
200	              <div className="net-modal-box">
201	                <p>Couldn&apos;t join: {connectError}</p>
202	                <button type="button" className="mc-button" onClick={() => setConnectError(null)}>
203	                  OK
204	                </button>
205	              </div>
206	            </div>
207	          )}
208	        </>
209	      );
210	    }
211	  }
212	
213	  return (

216	        setActiveProfile(profileId);

218	      }}
219	    />
220	  );
221	}

Advances the sync cursor. */\nexport async function pullSave(cloudWorldId: string, storage: Storage = localStorage): Promise<SaveData | null> {\n  try {\n    const response = await fetch(`/api/worlds/${cloudWorldId}/save`);\n    if (!response.ok) return null;\n    const stamp = response.headers.get(\"x-updated-at\");\n    const save = await gunzipJson<SaveData>(new Uint8Array(await response.arrayBuffer()));\n    if (stamp) writeStamp(cloudWorldId, stamp, storage);\n    return save;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}",
  "new_string": "/** Fetches the cloud blob + its stamp (null when the world has no blob yet or the fetch fails). */\nasync function fetchCloudSave(cloudWorldId: string): Promise<{ save: SaveData; updatedAt: string | null } | null> {\n  try {\n    const response = await fetch(`/api/worlds/${cloudWorldId}/save`);\n    if (!response.ok) return null;\n    const updatedAt = response.headers.get(\"x-updated-at\");\n    const save = await gunzipJson<SaveData>(new Uint8Array(await response.arrayBuffer()));\n    return { save, updatedAt };\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Downloads the latest cloud save (null when the world has no blob yet). Advances the sync cursor. */\nexport async function pullSave(cloudWorldId: string, storage: Storage = localStorage): Promise<SaveData | null> {\n  const result = await fetchCloudSave(cloudWorldId);\n  if (!result) return null;\n  if (result.updatedAt) writeStamp(cloudWorldId, result.updatedAt, storage);\n  return result.save;\n}\n\nexport type PullDecision = { adopt: true; save: SaveData } | { adopt: false };\n\n/**\n * Open-time reconcile: adopt the remote save ONLY when it advanced past what this\n * device last synced (its cursor). So re-opening a world you played offline keeps\n * your newer local progress instead of clobbering it with an older cloud copy;\n * a first download (no cursor yet) always adopts, and a genuine remote write from\n * another device wins (last-write-wins — the push side warns on the conflict).\n */\nexport async function pullCloudSaveIfNewer(cloudWorldId: string, storage: Storage = localStorage): Promise<PullDecision> {\n  const result = await fetchCloudSave(cloudWorldId);\n  if (!result) return { adopt: false }; // no blob yet, or offline → keep local\n  const cursor = readStamps(storage)[cloudWorldId];\n  if (result.updatedAt && result.updatedAt === cursor) return { adopt: false }; // unchanged since our last sync\n  if (result.updatedAt) writeStamp(cloudWorldId, result.updatedAt, storage);\n  return { adopt: true, save: result.save };\n}"
}

import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { gunzipJson, gzipJson } from "./cloudSaves";

describe("cloud save codec", () => {
  test("gzip round-trips a save-shaped object and actually compresses", async () => {
    const save = {
      version: 17,
      seed: 1337,
      changes: Array.from({ length: 2000 }, (_, i) => [i, i % 5]),
      players: [{ id: "local", hearts: 20 }]
    };
    const bytes = await gzipJson(save);
    // Repetitive block diffs are the whole payload story — they must shrink.
    expect(bytes.byteLength).toBeLessThan(JSON.stringify(save).length / 2);
    const back = await gunzipJson<typeof save>(bytes);
    expect(back).toEqual(save);
  });

  test("gunzip rejects garbage by throwing (callers catch to null)", async () => {
    await expect(gunzipJson(new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3]))).rejects.toBeDefined();
  });
});

{
  "command": "cd /Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft; cat >> lib/game/cloudSaves.test.ts <<'EOF'\n\ndescribe(\"pullCloudSaveIfNewer (open-time reconcile)\", () => {\n  const originalFetch = globalThis.fetch;\n  afterEach(() => {\n    globalThis.fetch = originalFetch;\n  });\n\n  const save = { version: 17, seed: 1, changes: [] } as unknown as SaveData;\n\n  /** Stub fetch to answer the cloud GET with a gzipped save + an x-updated-at header. */\n  function stubCloud(updatedAt: string | null, ok = true): void {\n    globalThis.fetch = (async () => {\n      const bytes = await gzipJson(save);\n      return {\n        ok,\n        headers: { get: (key: string) => (key === \"x-updated-at\" ? updatedAt : null) },\n        arrayBuffer: async () => bytes.buffer.slice(bytes.byteOffset, bytes.byteOffset + bytes.byteLength)\n      } as unknown as Response;\n    }) as typeof fetch;\n  }\n\n  test(\"first download (no cursor) adopts the remote save and records the stamp\", async () => {\n    const storage = fakeStorage();\n    stubCloud(\"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\");\n    const decision = await pullCloudSaveIfNewer(\"c1\", storage);\n    expect(decision.adopt).toBe(true);\n    if (decision.adopt) expect(decision.save.version).toBe(17);\n    expect(JSON.parse(storage.getItem(STAMPS_KEY)!).c1).toBe(\"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\");\n  });\n\n  test(\"keeps local when the remote is unchanged since this device's cursor\", async () => {\n    const storage = fakeStorage({ [STAMPS_KEY]: JSON.stringify({ c1: \"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\" }) });\n    stubCloud(\"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\"); // same stamp we last synced\n    expect((await pullCloudSaveIfNewer(\"c1\", storage)).adopt).toBe(false);\n  });\n\n  test(\"adopts when another device advanced the remote past the cursor\", async () => {\n    const storage = fakeStorage({ [STAMPS_KEY]: JSON.stringify({ c1: \"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\" }) });\n    stubCloud(\"2026-02-02T00:00:00Z\"); // newer than the cursor\n    expect((await pullCloudSaveIfNewer(\"c1\", storage)).adopt).toBe(true);\n  });\n\n  test(\"keeps local when the world has no blob yet or the fetch fails\", async () => {\n    const storage = fakeStorage();\n    stubCloud(null, false);\n    expect((await pullCloudSaveIfNewer(\"c1\", storage)).adopt).toBe(false);\n  });\n});\nEOF\necho done",
  "description": "Append pullCloudSaveIfNewer tests"
}
