20:## React shell (`lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `components/`)
22:- `useMinecraftGame` creates the `GameEngine` in the canvas mount's callback ref, then an effect builds the `GameRenderer`, the `AudioDirector`, and `inputController` and drives the `requestAnimationFrame` loop: `engine.step(dt, input)` (in bounded catch-up substeps of ≤50 ms via `createAccumulator` from `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts`, so slow frames — e.g. software GL — don't run the simulation in slow motion) → drain engine events (death/respawn handling, `attackSwung` → `renderer.triggerSwing()`, + `renderer.handleEvent` for particle bursts, + `audio.handleEvent`) → `minimap.sync(state)` → `renderer.sync(state)` → `audio.sync(state, dt)` → `renderer.render()`. The minimap must sync **before** the renderer because it reads `state.worldMeshDirty`, which `renderer.sync` clears.
23:- `components/GameShell.tsx` is the menu shell **above** `useMinecraftGame`: a profile-select → world-select → play state machine (profiles own worlds; see [save-format.md](save-format.md)) that runs the one-time legacy migration on mount and renders `MinecraftGame` keyed by `world.id` (+ a reload nonce). Switching worlds, Load, or Reset changes the key, so React unmounts the game subtree — running the effect cleanup that disposes renderer/audio/input and clears the rAF + autosave — and a fresh mount boots the next world, **no page reload**. The tab's active world is remembered in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes it while a fresh tab cold-starts at the menu. `useMinecraftGame` therefore takes the `world` + `profile` to play and persists to that world's own `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key.
31:- Note for the React Compiler lint rules: consume the hook with destructuring (`const { … } = useMinecraftGame()`); property access on the result object can false-positive `react-hooks/refs`.
45:0. Pause gate: while `state.paused`, `step` refreshes the snapshot and returns — mobs, the day clock, mining, and stats all freeze (autosave still serializes fine)
68:**Game modes.** The four modes (`survival`/`creative`/`adventure`/`spectator`, `lib/game/gameModes.ts`) are a single `state.gameMode` axis. Systems gate on **intent predicates** rather than the raw id, so all four share one set of seams: `takesDamage` switches off the three damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts` (covering fall/void/lava/water/drown/mob/poison at once) plus hunger/regen/oxygen in `playerStats.ts`; `canEditBlocks`/`freeBuild` gate breaking and placing in `mining.ts`; `canInteract` gates the interaction commands in `dispatch`; `canFly`/`isNoclip` drive flight and the collision skip in `playerMotion.ts` (and the auto-unstuck skip in `step`); `mobsThreaten` folds into `activeHostile` in `mobAI.ts`; `usesInventory`/`takesDamage` hide HUD elements. `gameMode` rides the per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` → a v8 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`), but unlike `worldType` it's **switchable in-game** — `setGameMode` (`GameEngine.switchGameMode`) resets transient hazard timers, bars, flight, and noclip-entombment on the change. The transient `isFlying` is never serialized.
70:**Difficulty.** Orthogonal to the mode, `state.difficulty` (`peaceful`/`easy`/`normal`/`hard`, `lib/game/difficulties.ts`) decides _how hard_ survival is — it follows the same shape as game modes: an enum, an `isDifficulty` guard, `DIFFICULTY_PRESETS` for the UI, and **accessor functions** (`hostilesSpawn`, `mobDamageMultiplier`, `hostileSpawnIntervalScale`, `hostileCapScale`, `regenIntervalScale`, `starves`/`starvationFloorHp`) that systems read instead of the raw id. The seams: `spawnDirector.ts` gates the initial population + night director + dungeon spawners on `hostilesSpawn` and scales the cadence/cap; `mobAI.ts` multiplies every mob hit at the strike (templates untouched); `playerStats.ts` scales regen and runs the new **starvation** tick (hunger 0 chips to a per-level HP floor, lethal only on Hard, routed through the same floored/lethal damage paths as Poison/environment). Difficulty rides the same per-world plumbing as `gameMode` (`WorldMeta` → a v9 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`) and is switchable in-game — `setDifficulty` (`GameEngine.switchDifficulty`) just updates the value the directors read next tick, except dropping to Peaceful, which despawns the hostiles already present (a plain splice — no loot/XP, no false boss victory). The two axes don't cross-couple: spawning keys only on difficulty, threat/damage only on mode.
72:**Hardcore.** A per-world boolean (`state.hardcore`, persisted in save v10 + `WorldMeta`, **immutable** unlike mode/difficulty). The constructor resolves it first so it overrides the other axes — forced to Survival + Hard — and `switchGameMode`/`switchDifficulty` early-return under it (the player-facing switchers are disabled; the engine's own death transition sets the mode directly, bypassing the lock). Death is permanent: the two lethal seams (`applyDamage`, `applyEnvironmentalDamage`) divert to `GameEngine.triggerGameOver()`, which sets the persisted `gameOver` flag and flips the player to **Spectator** (a free-cam over the dead world, invulnerable so mobs can't re-trigger it) instead of arming the respawn countdown — so a reloaded `gameOver` world boots straight into spectating (the constructor resolves `gameMode` to spectator; the existing `!isNoclip` stuck-check leaves it un-teleported). The shell force-saves on the `gameOver` event so a tab-close still persists the dead world; the Game Over screen (`components/game/GameOverScreen.tsx`) owns navigation (spectate / quit / delete), and `pause` is blocked while `gameOver`. The hearts render in a withered palette (`lib/ui/hudPixels.ts`).
109:- Volume settings (`settings.ts`) persist under their own localStorage key (`minecraft_audio_v1`) — never part of the world save.
119:Online play mounts the **same** shell/renderer/audio/input stack on a different engine: `connectNetworkSession(url, ticket)` (`NetworkSession.ts`) performs the hello → welcome → gzipped world-sync handshake, then constructs a **replica** engine (`replica: true, bootPlayer: false` — worldgen from the server's seed is byte-identical thanks to `lib/world/noise.ts`, the world sync applies the block diff/containers/mobs on top). `useMinecraftGame` accepts the session via its `online` option: the replica engine is mounted instead of constructing one, localStorage persistence is skipped (the server owns the world), replicated server events join the local event drain (so toasts/audio/particles treat them like local ones), and `session.afterFrame` runs each rAF.
```

Reuses the \"Opening…\" modal.\n- Conflict: a losing push (409) warns once and stops syncing rather than\n  overwriting the other device; the next open adopts their newer save.\nEOF\ngit log --oneline -1 && echo \"=== push ===\" && git push 2>&1 | tail -3",

### components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx:142
_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**`pushSave` result is never checked before treating the world as synced.**

`linkWorldCloud` runs, and the card flips to "☁ Synced," regardless of whether `pushSave` returns `"saved"`, `"conflict"`, or `"error"`. On a failed/conflicting push, the local world is linked to an empty (or stale) cloud row while the UI claims it's synced — a real risk for data loss if the user then relies on that badge across devices.

1. **`GameShell.downloadCloud` double-click race** — `createWorld()` runs before `playLocal`'s `joiningRef` guard, so a fast second click persists a duplicate local world with the same `cloudId`.

  "old_string": "  // \"Upload to cloud\": create an sp-cloud world row, link it to this local world,\n  // and push the current save. Re-renders (setUploading) re-read the manifest so\n  // the card flips to \"Synced\".\n  const uploadToCloud = (world: WorldMeta) => {\n    setUploadError(null);\n    setUploading(world.id);\n    const save = readSave(worldSaveKey(world.id));\n    void createOnlineWorld({\n      name: world.name,\n      seed: world.seed,\n      worldType: world.worldType,\n      gameMode: world.gameMode,\n      difficulty: world.difficulty,\n      hardcore: world.hardcore,\n      kind: \"sp-cloud\"\n    }).then(async (cloud) => {\n      if (!cloud) {\n        setUploading(null);\n        setUploadError(world.id); // keep the world local — surface the failure\n        return;\n      }\n      linkWorldCloud(world.id, cloud.id);\n      if (save) await pushSave(cloud.id, save);\n      refreshOnline();\n      setUploading(null);\n    });\n  };",
  "new_string": "  const without = (set: ReadonlySet<string>, id: string) => {\n    const next = new Set(set);\n    next.delete(id);\n    return next;\n  };\n\n  // \"Upload to cloud\": create an sp-cloud world row, push the current save, and —\n  // only if the push actually lands — link it so the card flips to \"Synced\".\n  // Linking on a failed push would falsely claim the (empty) cloud row is synced.\n  const uploadToCloud = (world: WorldMeta) => {\n    setUploadError((prev) => without(prev, world.id));\n    setUploading((prev) => new Set(prev).add(world.id));\n    const save = readSave(worldSaveKey(world.id));\n    void createOnlineWorld({\n      name: world.name,\n      seed: world.seed,\n      worldType: world.worldType,\n      gameMode: world.gameMode,\n      difficulty: world.difficulty,\n      hardcore: world.hardcore,\n      kind: \"sp-cloud\"\n    }).then(async (cloud) => {\n      // A world with no local save yet has nothing to push — link it now and let\n      // the first play autosave upload the blob.\n      const pushed = cloud && save ? await pushSave(cloud.id, save) : \"saved\";\n      if (cloud && pushed === \"saved\") {\n        linkWorldCloud(world.id, cloud.id);\n        refreshOnline();\n      } else {\n        setUploadError((prev) => new Set(prev).add(world.id)); // keep the world local — surface the failure\n      }\n      setUploading((prev) => without(prev, world.id));\n    });\n  };"
}

({ ok: false, status: 500 } as Response) // creating the cloud row fails\n        : ({ ok: true, json: async () => ({ worlds: [] }) } as unknown as Response)) as typeof fetch;\n    try {\n      const user = userEvent.setup();\n      createWorld(\"p1\", \"Local\", \"1\", { uid: () => \"wl\" });\n      render(<WorldSelect profile={PROFILE} onPlay={mock()} onPlayOnline={() => {}} onDownloadCloud={() => {}} onBack={mock()} />);\n\n      await user.click(await screen.findByRole(\"button\", { name: \"Upload to cloud\" }));\n\n      // The upload failed → the button reports it, the world was NOT linked, no false badge.\n      expect(await screen.findByRole(\"button\", { name: \"Upload failed\" })).toBeTruthy();\n      expect(screen.queryByText(/Synced/)).toBeNull();\n      expect(readWorlds().worlds.find((w) => w.id === \"wl\")?.cloudId).toBeUndefined();\n    } finally {\n      globalThis.fetch = originalFetch;\n    }\n  });\n});"

> AGENT

Here's my honest read on where things stand and what's worth doing next.

## The lay of the land

MP v2 (v0.14.0) is **built and in review** — PR #44, all four phases + the CodeRabbit fixes, CI green. You've paused the release, so the co-op work is "done but not landed." Everything else on the board:

- **Close-out items for MP v2** (your timing): a real 2-browser gameplay pass on the new features, redeploy the Fly server to protocol v2, then merge + cut v0.14.0. The gameplay pass is the one recurring debt in this project — the roadmap notes it's been deferred every release, and the wolf/cat spawn bug that shipped is exactly the kind a manual pass catches. MP v2 has the *most* unverified surface yet (boat physics in MP, arrow visuals, kill-credit feel, kick UX, cross-device cloud sync).
- **New content**: a menu of deferred thrusts — a potions/enchants batch (Fire Aspect/Thorns/Night Vision/splash — quick wins on existing seams), a **drowned** hostile (leans on the aquatic update), rideable **mounts** (which would reuse the exact vehicle mount/ride/replication machinery I just extended for MP — high synergy, MP-ready almost for free), or bigger swings (Nether-like dimension, redstone-lite, slabs/stairs).
- **Housekeeping**: the agreed **MIT license** (small upstream PR first, then the fork adopts), and the parked dev "inventory-loss-on-reload" bug (blocked on your console dump).

## What I think

My honest recommendation: **harden and verify MP v2 before piling more on top of it.** It's a large, freshly-landed, mostly-unverified stack, and the highest-leverage thing I can actually do (a true 2-browser manual pass is your job, but I *can* extend the Playwright multiplayer e2e to drive the new features end-to-end — board a boat together, see arrows replicate, each earn a distinct advancement, owner-kick, a cloud-save round-trip). That's the automated version of the pass that keeps slipping, and it de-risks the merge/release. Building the next feature on an unverified multiplayer base is how compounding bugs happen.

That said, if you'd rather keep momentum on content, **mounts** is the standout next feature — it reuses everything I just built.

Which direction do you want to point at?

1	import { expect, test, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
2	import { acquirePointerLock } from "./helpers";
3	
4	/**
5	 * The full co-op journey against the real online stack: the Next app backed
6	 * by an in-process Postgres (DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory) plus the Bun game
7	 * server, both from playwright.config's webServer list — no Docker, no cloud.
8	 * Two isolated browser contexts play two guests: the host creates an online
9	 * world through the menus, the friend joins through the invite link, and the
10	 * pair must see each other, share block edits, and chat.
11	 */
12	
13	/** Console/page errors collected like the smoke fixture does (favicon 404 is noise). */
14	function watchErrors(page: Page, sink: string[]): void {
15	  page.on("console", (message) => {
16	    if (message.type() !== "error") return;
17	    if (message.text().includes("Failed to load resource") && message.location().url.endsWith("/favicon.ico")) return;
18	    sink.push(`${message.text()} (${message.location().url})`);
19	  });
20	  page.on("pageerror", (error) => sink.push(String(error)));
21	}
22	
23	/** Booted, synced, and drawing: the bar every online entry must clear. */
24	async function waitForOnlineGame(page: Page): Promise<void> {
25	  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft !== undefined, undefined, { timeout: 30000 });
26	  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft!.net?.status() === "online", undefined, { timeout: 30000 });
27	  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft!.renderer.renderedTriangles() > 0, undefined, { timeout: 30000 });
28	}
29

32	  // renders with software GL, so the whole journey gets a generous ceiling.
33	  test.setTimeout(240000);
34	  const errors: string[] = [];
35	
36	  // ── the host: guest account → online world → in-game ─────────────────────
37	  const hostContext = await browser.newContext();

39	  watchErrors(host, errors);
40	  // Seed a profile so the menu opens on the profile LIST (where the account
41	  // panel lives) instead of the first-run create form.
42	  await host.addInitScript(() => {
43	    if (!localStorage.getItem("minecraft_profiles_v1")) {
44	      localStorage.setItem(
45	        "minecraft_profiles_v1",
46	        JSON.stringify({ version: 1, profiles: [{ id: "host-profile", name: "Hosta", skinId: "default", createdAt: 1 }], activeProfileId: "host-profile" })
47	      );
48	    }
49	  });
50	  await host.goto("/");
51	
52	  await host.getByRole("button", { name: "Play online as guest" }).click();
53	  await expect(host.getByText("Playing as guest")).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 });
54	  await host.getByTestId("profile-host-profile").click();
55	
56	  // Creative, so the host's block breaks are instant on the server side.
57	  await host.getByTestId("new-online-world").click();
58	  await host.getByLabel("World name").fill("Co-op Test");
59	  await host.getByLabel("World seed").fill("4242");
60	  await host.getByRole("button", { name: "Creative mode" }).click();
61	  await host.getByRole("button", { name: "Create World" }).click();
62	  await waitForOnlineGame(host);
63	
64	  // Mint the invite with the host's cookies (the menu's Copy button wraps the
65	  // same endpoint; the clipboard is out of reach in headless runs).
66	  const worldId = await host.evaluate(async () => {

69	    return worlds[0].id;

73	    const { token } = (await response.json()) as { token: string };

90	  await waitForOnlineGame(friend);
91	
92	  // ── both replicas agree there are two players in the room ────────────────
93	  for (const page of [host, friend]) {
94	    await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft!.engine.state.players.size === 2, undefined, { timeout: 15000 });
95	  }
96	
97	  // ── a block edit crosses the wire ─────────────────────────────────────────
98	  // The host digs straight down. The replica's own mining is cosmetic (it

100	  // clients proves the server decided the break and broadcast it.
101	  await acquirePointerLock(host);

109	  }

111	
112	  // ── chat round-trips, rendering in the other player's log ────────────────
113	  await host.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft!.net!.sendChat("hello from the host"));
114	  await expect(friend.getByText("hello from the host")).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10000 });
115	  await friend.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft!.net!.sendChat("hi back"));
116	  await expect(host.getByText("hi back")).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10000 });
117	
118	  expect(errors, "no console/page errors during the test").toEqual([]);
119	  await hostContext.close();
120	  await friendContext.close();
121	});

# Harden & verify MP v2 — end-to-end browser coverage for the new co-op features

## Context

MP v2 (PR #44, branch `feat/mp-v2`, all 4 phases + review fixes) is thoroughly covered by **unit/integration** tests (1107 pass), but the **browser e2e** still only exercises v1: `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` drives invite → join → shared block-edit → chat, and nothing more. The new co-op surface — **owner kick / roster**, **arrow replication**, and **SP cloud saves** — has no end-to-end browser coverage.

This matters because this project's one recurring quality debt is the **perpetually-deferred manual gameplay pass** (the shipped wolf/cat spawn bug is the cautionary tale — unit tests passed because fixtures built the mobs directly; only a real play session would have caught it). A true 2-browser visual pass stays the user's job, but the practically-drivable new behaviors *can* be locked with automated e2e — the automated version of that pass. Adding it **de-risks the eventual merge/release** of a large, freshly-landed feature and lands the coverage **on `feat/mp-v2` so PR #44 itself gains it**.

**Verified during exploration:** the Phase 3 session API (`net.role`, `net.roster()`, `net.kick()`, `net.subscribeRoster()`) and the cloud-save testids (`cloud-world-<id>`) already exist, so **no app code changes are needed** — this is pure test authoring against the documented `window.__monecraft.{engine,net,renderer}` hooks and existing selectors.

## Approach

Add to **`feat/mp-v2`** (part of PR #44), not a new branch. Two pieces: extend the existing co-op journey test, and add a focused cloud-save spec. All driving goes through `window.__monecraft` and existing roles/testids, mirroring the patterns already in `multiplayer.e2e.ts`.

### 1. Extend `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` (the one co-op journey test) — roster, arrows, kick

The existing test already creates a **Creative** online world with two guests in it. Append three checks to that same flow (one expensive setup, reused). **Kick must be last** — it disconnects the friend.

- **Roster** (after the `players.size === 2` gate): assert `net.roster().length === 2` on both pages, and that the host — an **owner** — renders a Kick button: `host.getByRole("button", { name: /^Kick / })` visible (the `RosterPanel` owner control, `components/game/RosterPanel.tsx:30`). This proves `role`/`roster()`/`subscribeRoster` end-to-end and the owner-only UI gate.

- **Arrow replication** (Creative world → the `creativeGiveItem` hook, no pointer aiming needed): on the host,
  1. Aim roughly level so the arrow flies instead of burying instantly: `host.evaluate(() => { window.__monecraft.engine.state.player.pitch = 0; })`, brief settle.
  2. `engine.dispatch({ type: "creativeGiveItem", itemId: "bow" })` and `"arrow"` (both cross the wire — `protocol.ts` allow-list; server-side give lands at the player's `selectedSlot`, `GameEngine.ts` creative-give handler).
  3. `expect.poll` the self-delta'd inventory for the bow slot (`inventory.findIndex(s => s?.id === "bow")`), then `dispatch({ type: "selectSlot", index: <bowSlot> })`; `expect.poll` that an `arrow` is present too.
  4. `dispatch({ type: "attack" })` — the server fires the bow (`tryFireBow` needs a held bow + ≥1 arrow).
  5. Assert on **both** pages: `expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.engine.state.projectiles.length)).toBeGreaterThan(0)` — proving the `prj` channel replicates the arrow to the remote replica.
  - This is the fiddliest check (inventory sync latency + short arrow lifetime). If it proves flaky, fall back to asserting the host-side spawn plus a `mobsKeyframe`-independent friend-side poll with a longer window; worst case, drop it and rely on the `prj` unit tests (`server/room.test.ts` broadcast + `NetworkSession.test.ts` upsert). Flag it in the commit if trimmed.

- **Owner kick** (final gameplay step, before the `errors` assertion): get the friend's id from the host roster (`net.roster().find(m => m.id !== net.playerId).id`), then `host.evaluate(id => window.__monecraft.net.kick(id), friendId)` — exactly what the RosterPanel button's `onClick` calls. Assert:
  - friend: `expect.poll(() => friend.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.net.status())).toBe("closed")` **and** `friend.getByRole("alertdialog", { name: "Disconnected" })` visible (the `net-modal` from `ConnectionStatus.tsx:24` on a fatal `CLOSE_KICKED`, which is in `FATAL_CLOSES` → no reconnect).
  - host: `expect.poll(() => host.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.engine.state.players.size)).toBe(1)`.
  - **Risk to check:** a server-initiated `4003` close should be a clean browser close (no console error), so the terminal `expect(errors).toEqual([])` still holds. If the browser logs a WS-close error, extend `watchErrors`'s filter (the same pattern it already uses for favicon 404s).

### 2. New `e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts` — the SP cloud round-trip (menu flow, no game server)

Cloud saves are the **WorldSelect menu** against `/api/worlds` (the Next app + pglite) — no WS session. One signed-in guest, one context, simulating a second device by clearing the sync cursor:

1. Seed a profile via `addInitScript` (like the MP test), `goto("/")`, **"Play online as guest"** → "Playing as guest", click the profile.

The plan notes this gap explicitly rather than shipping a flaky boarding e2e.

- **`e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts`** (new) — the guest-signin → create → play/edit → upload → delete → clear-cursor → download → assert-edit-survived round-trip. Reuse the profile-seed + guest-signin patterns from `multiplayer.e2e.ts` and the break-block pattern from `e2e/smoke.e2e.ts`.

=== helpers.ts ===
import { test as base, expect, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
import { WORLDGEN_VERSION } from "@/lib/game/config";

/**
 * Shared E2E plumbing. Tests assert against the live simulation through the
 * window.__monecraft debug handle rather than pixels — see docs/testing.md.
 */

export const test = base.extend<{ gamePage: Page }>({
  // A page that has booted the game, with console errors treated as failures.
  // (The fixture continuation is named `runTest`, not Playwright's
  // conventional `use`, to avoid colliding with React's rules-of-hooks lint.)
  gamePage: async ({ page }, runTest) => {
    const errors: string[] = [];
    page.on("console", (message) => {
      if (message.type() !== "error") return;
      // The app ships no favicon; Chrome's automatic /favicon.ico 404 is noise.
      if (message.text().includes("Failed to load resource") && message.location().url.endsWith("/favicon.ico")) return;
      errors.push(`${message.text()} (${message.location().url})`);
    });
    page.on("pageerror", (error) => errors.push(String(error)));

    // Seed a known profile + world so the menu has something to enter. Runs on
    // every navigation (including reloads), but only fills the manifests when
    // absent so a test's own writes survive a reload.
    await page.addInitScript((worldgenVersion) => {
      if (!localStorage.getItem("minecraft_profiles_v1")) {
        localStorage.setItem(
          "minecraft_profiles_v1",
          JSON.stringify({ version: 1, profiles: [{ id: "e2e-profile", name: "Tester", skinId: "default", createdAt: 1 }], activeProfileId: "e2e-profile" })
        );
      }
      if (!localStorage.getItem("minecraft_worlds_v1")) {
        localStorage.setItem(
          "minecraft_worlds_v1",
          JSON.stringify({
            version: 1,
            worlds: [{ id: "e2e-world", profileId: "e2e-profile", name: "Test World", seed: 1337, worldgenVersion, createdAt: 1, lastPlayedAt: 1 }]
          })
        );
      }
    }, WORLDGEN_VERSION);

    await page.goto("/");
    // Enter the world through the menu (first load only; reloads auto-resume the tab's world).
    await page.getByTestId("profile-e2e-profile").click();
    await page.getByTestId("world-e2e-world").click();
    await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft !== undefined, undefined, { timeout: 30000 });
    // Wait for the first frames so the engine has stepped and the scene drew.
    await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft!.renderer.renderedTriangles() > 0, undefined, { timeout: 30000 });

    await runTest(page);

    expect(errors, "no console/page errors during the test").toEqual([]);
  }
});

export { expect };

/**
 * The game boots at dawn with aggro hostiles near the spawn; interactive
 * tests clear them and move to midday so knockback can't disrupt input.
 */
export async function calmDaytime(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const state = window.__monecraft!.engine.state;
    state.mobs = state.mobs.filter((mob) => !mob.hostile);
    state.dayClock = 60;
  });
}

export async function playerPosition(page: Page): Promise<{ x: number; y: number; z: number }> {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const { position } = window.__monecraft!.engine.state.player;
    return { x: position.x, y: position.y, z: position.z };
  });
}

/**
 * Double-clicks the canvas to request pointer lock; if the browser refuses
 * (headless Chromium cannot engage pointer lock at all), forces the input
 * controller's lock flag so everything downstream — keys → engine, held mouse
 * → mining — is still exercised for real. The acquisition UX itself stays in
 * the manual gameplay pass.
 */
export async function acquirePointerLock(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  const canvas = page.locator(".game-canvas-wrap canvas");
  await canvas.dblclick();
  try {
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.pointerLockElement !== null, undefined, { timeout: 2000 });
  } catch {
    await page.evaluate(() => {
      window.__monecraft!.input.forcePointerLock(true);
    });
  }
}

export async function itemCount(page: Page, itemId: string): Promise<number> {
  return page.evaluate((id) => window.__monecraft!.engine.state.inventory.filter((slot) => slot.id === id).reduce((sum, slot) => sum + slot.count, 0), itemId);
}

test("holding the mouse mines the block underfoot", async ({ gamePage: page }) => {
  await calmDaytime(page);
  await acquirePointerLock(page);
  await page.waitForTimeout(1000); // settle (slow CI renderers need the margin)

  // Aim straight down from the center of the cell (a ray origin exactly on a
  // cell boundary may target the diagonal neighbor — see docs/testing.md).
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const { player } = window.__monecraft!.engine.state;
    player.pitch = -Math.PI / 2 + 0.02;
    player.position.x = Math.floor(player.position.x) + 0.5;
    player.position.z = Math.floor(player.position.z) + 0.5;
  });

  await page.mouse.down();
  // Generous timeout: CI renders with software GL at single-digit FPS.
  await expect.poll(async () => page.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft!.engine.state.blockChanges.changes().length), { timeout: 30000 }).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  await page.mouse.up();
});

test("right-click still places a block when not aimed at an interactive one", async ({ gamePage: page }) => {
  // The bed/furnace interact dispatcher sits in front of placement; this guards
  // that a non-interactive target still falls through to placing a block.
  await calmDaytime(page);
  await acquirePointerLock(page);
  await page.waitForTimeout(1000); // settle

  // Carve a clear lane ending in a stone backstop, dead ahead at eye height.
  const placed = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const state = window.__monecraft!.engine.state;
    const ex = Math.floor(state.player.position.x);
    const ez = Math.floor(state.player.position.z);
    state.player.position.x = ex + 0.5;
    state.player.position.z = ez + 0.5;
    state.player.yaw = 0;
    state.player.pitch = 0;
    const ey = Math.floor(state.player.position.y + 1.62);
    // 1 = Grass, 0 = Air, 3 = Stone (BlockId enum values).
    state.blockChanges.set(ex, ey, ez - 1, 0);
    state.blockChanges.set(ex, ey, ez - 2, 0);
    state.blockChanges.set(ex, ey, ez - 3, 3);
    state.selectedSlot = 0; // starter grass blocks
    const before = state.world.get(ex, ey, ez - 2);
    window.__monecraft!.engine.dispatch({ type: "placeBlock" });
    const after = state.world.get(ex, ey, ez - 2);
    return { before, after };
  });
  expect(placed.before).toBe(0); // air

export function createInitialInventory(): InventorySlot[] {
  const slots: InventorySlot[] = Array.from({ length: INVENTORY_SLOTS }, () => createEmptySlot());
  const starter: Array<{ id: string; count: number }> = [
    { id: "grass", count: 64 },
    { id: "dirt", count: 64 },
    { id: "stone", count: 64 },
    { id: "wood", count: 64 },
    { id: "planks", count: 20 },
    { id: "cobble", count: 20 },
    { id: "sand", count: 20 },
    { id: "wood_pickaxe", count: 1 },
    { id: "knife", count: 1 }
  ];
  for (let i = 0; i < starter.length && i < slots.length; i += 1) slots[i] = createSlot(starter[i].id, starter[i].count);
  return slots;
}
```

```
export function moveStack(a: InventorySlot[], indexA: number, b: InventorySlot[], indexB: number): { a: InventorySlot[]; b: InventorySlot[] } | null {
  if (a === b) {
    const swapped = swapSlots(a, indexA, indexB);
    return swapped ? { a: swapped, b: swapped } : null;
  }
  if (indexA < 0 || indexA >= a.length || indexB < 0 || indexB >= b.length) return null;
  const nextA = cloneSlots(a);
  const nextB = cloneSlots(b);
  const temp = nextA[indexA];
  nextA[indexA] = nextB[indexB];
  nextB[indexB] = temp;
  return { a: nextA, b: nextB };
}
```

 */
export function tryFireBow(state: GameState, player: PlayerState, emit: EmitGameEvent, rng?: () => number): boolean {
  const slot = player.inventory[player.selectedSlot];
  if (!isBow(slot)) return false;
  if (player.timers.bowCooldownTimer > 0) return false;
  if ((countsById(player.inventory).get("arrow") ?? 0) < 1) return false;

  const { position, yaw, pitch } = player;
  scratchOrigin.set(position.x, position.y + EYE_HEIGHT, position.z);
  lookDirection(yaw, pitch, scratchForward);
  // Power and Punch are bow-only enchants, read off the held bow at the one fire seam.
  spawnArrow(state, scratchOrigin.x, scratchOrigin.y, scratchOrigin.z, scratchForward, {
    speed: ARROW_SPEED,
    damage: BOW_ARROW_DAMAGE + powerBonus(slot),
    knockback: BOW_KNOCKBACK + punchKnockback(slot),
    fromPlayer: true,
    owner: player.id, // kill credit follows the shooter
    ttl: ARROW_TTL
  });

  player.inventory = adjustSlotCount(player.inventory, "arrow", -1) ?? player.inventory;
  player.inventory = consumeToolDurability(player.inventory, player.selectedSlot, BOW_DURABILITY_PER_SHOT, rng) ?? player.inventory;
  player.timers.bowCooldownTimer = BOW_COOLDOWN_SECONDS;
```

The diagnostic is the key: `arrows` dropped 99→98 (the bow **did** fire) but `proj: 0`. The arrow despawned on its very first server tick — `room.tick` runs `engine.step` (which ticks/collides the arrow) *before* `collectProjectilePoses`, so a fast arrow that hits terrain immediately never gets broadcast. Firing near-**straight up** into open sky keeps it airborne across ticks so it replicates. Let me fix that and remove the diagnostic:

Done. The e2e hardening is committed and pushed to PR #44.

## What landed (`2323a73`)

Automated browser coverage for the new MP v2 co-op surface — the automated stand-in for the manual pass that keeps getting deferred:

- **`multiplayer.e2e.ts`** (the co-op journey) now also asserts: both replicas list a **roster of two** and only the owner renders a **Kick** control; then the owner **kicks** the friend, who lands on the disconnect modal while the host's player count drops to one.
- **`cloudSaves.e2e.ts`** (new): a full single-player **cloud round-trip** — create a local world, place a distinctive block, Upload to cloud, delete the local copy, clear the device's sync cursor (simulating a fresh device), Download from Cloud Saves, and confirm the block survived the push → delete → pull cycle.

No app changes — it all drives through hooks/selectors that already existed. **Full e2e suite green (21 passed), run 3× cleanly.**

## Two honest notes

- **Arrow replication was dropped from e2e** and stays unit-tested. Driving it end-to-end fought too many systems (creative mode, inventory juggling, arrow physics, timing) to be reliable — and a flaky test undermines the whole point. The `prj` channel is solidly covered in `server/room.test.ts` + `NetworkSession.test.ts`.
- Chasing it **surfaced a real (cosmetic) product gap**: `room.tick` runs the engine step — which can collide and despawn a fast arrow — *before* it collects poses, so a bow shot that hits on its very first tick never broadcasts. A point-blank arrow won't show mid-flight (its hit effect still replicates). I left it as-is and documented it; it's the kind of thing this verification pass exists to catch.

## Where PR #44 stands

All four MP v2 phases + review fixes + this e2e hardening are on the branch, CI green. 🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts (1)
`29-104`: _🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🔵 Trivial_ | _⚡ Quick win_
**Wrap the test body in try/finally to guarantee `context.close()` on failure.**
`context.close()` (Line 103) only runs if every prior assertion passes. If any `expect(...)` in the upload/delete/download flow throws, the manually-created context is never closed, leaking a browser context for the rest of the worker's lifetime. Playwright's own docs note it's best practice to explicitly close contexts created via `browser.newContext()` when done with them.
🔧 Proposed fix
```diff
   const context = await browser.newContext();
-  const page = await context.newPage();
-  watchErrors(page, errors);
-  ...
-  expect(errors, "no console/page errors during the test").toEqual([]);
-  await context.close();
+  try {
+    const page = await context.newPage();
+    watchErrors(page, errors);
+    ...
+    expect(errors, "no console/page errors during the test").toEqual([]);
+  } finally {
+    await context.close();
+  }
 });
```

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Finish landing MP v2 — redeploy the game server to protocol v2

## Context

MP v2 merged to `main` with **PROTOCOL_VERSION 1 → 2**. Vercel auto-deployed the v2 web app to production, but the Fly game server (`monecraft-server`) still runs **v1** — and the protocol is hard-version-locked both ways, so the live server now *cleanly refuses* online play (a v2 web client's hello/ticket carries `pv=2`, which the v1 server rejects). Single-player is unaffected. This closes that gap: redeploy the Fly server to v2 so production online co-op works again, then verify the full stack. That unblocks the manual gameplay pass on the live deploy and the v0.14.0 release cut (both your call, not part of this).

Prod has ~no active users and the refusal is clean-by-design, so this is low-risk housekeeping — but leaving the deploy half-shipped is untidy, so it's the responsible next step before new feature work.

## Approach

Pure ops — **no code changes**. Deploy `main`'s `server/` (which already carries `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 2`, `lib/net/protocol.ts:20`) to Fly using the committed config, then verify. Reuses the exact runbook in [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md).

1. **Prereqs** (read-only): we're on `main`, synced (done). Confirm `flyctl` is authed — `fly auth whoami` (`fly`/`flyctl` is installed at `/opt/homebrew/bin/fly`). If it's not logged in, you auth via `! fly auth login` before I proceed. The app's secrets (`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`, `DATABASE_URL`, `PORT`, `PERSISTENCE`) were set on the v0.13.0 deploy and **persist across a redeploy** — nothing to re-set, so no risk of the "#1 misconfiguration" (a `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` mismatch → close 4000).

2. **Deploy** (outward-facing, run after your go-ahead): from the repo root,
   `fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile`
   — builds and ships `main`'s v2 server code to `monecraft-server`. Fly does a rolling release; the version-lock means any lingering v1 client is refused cleanly during the swap (exactly what the bump was designed for).

3. **Verify** (no shared secret needed):
   - `curl https://monecraft-server.fly.dev/health` → `{"ok":true,"rooms":…}` (server up).
   - **Confirm it actually speaks v2** with a tiny WebSocket probe (only close codes, so no ticket/secret required): a `hello { protocol: 2, ticket: "bogus" }` must close with **4000** (bad ticket — the protocol matched the door), while a `hello { protocol: 1, … }` must close with **4001** (protocol mismatch). The server checks `message.protocol !== PROTOCOL_VERSION` *before* the ticket (`server/index.ts`), so those two close codes distinguish a v2 server from a v1 one. (`scripts/netProbe.ts` is the existing full handshake probe — reference for the WS client shape.)

## Critical files / commands

- `server/fly.toml`, `server/Dockerfile` — the committed deploy config (unchanged).
- `scripts/netProbe.ts` — the existing WS probe used for the v0.13.0 prod validation (reference for the close-code check).
- [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md) — the runbook this follows (deploy command, health check, troubleshooting table).

## Verification

- `fly deploy` reports a successful release; `/health` returns 200 `{"ok":true}`; the WS close-code probe confirms the deployed server is v2 (4000 on `protocol:2`+bad ticket, 4001 on `protocol:1`).
- Definitive end-to-end confirmation is the **manual pass** below: open `https://monecraft.vercel.app`, guest sign-in → create an online world → it connects (WELCOME).

## Out of scope (your timing, unblocked by this)

- The **manual 2-browser gameplay pass** on the live deploy — board a boat together, see arrows fly, each earn a distinct advancement, kick a guest, open a cloud world on a second device. (Not headless-automatable; the recurring project debt.)
- Cutting **v0.14.0** — version bump + roll `CHANGELOG [Unreleased] → [0.14.0]` + `chore(release)` commit + annotated tag, matching the v0.13.0 flow.

```

# Bun is pinned (not "latest") for reproducibility. Since worldgen v11 the pin
# is no longer load-bearing for the worldgen hash tests — seed-determined noise
# is bit-portable across JS engines (lib/world/noise.ts, proven by
# e2e/determinism.e2e.ts) — so a Bun bump should NOT shift those digests; if it
# ever does, that's a portability bug, not a re-baseline. See docs/testing.md.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.12"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bun run lint
      - run: bun run typecheck
      - run: bun run format:check
      - run: bun test
      - run: bun run build
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"

  e2e:
